projects.readme: # KidneyScan · Kidney CT research workspace KidneyScan is a local Flask app for exploring how image classifiers score a kidney CT slice. Upload a JPEG or PNG to see the predicted class, ranked raw scores, image details, and a model-attention overlay when available. The workspace uses a **four-class CNN** for Normal, Tumor, Stone, and Cyst when its checkpoint is present. With the bundled VGG16 checkpoint, it supports **Normal and Tumor**. Both use the same upload and result workflow. **Research use only.** Scores are uncalibrated. The app accepts ordinary image files and cannot verify that an upload is a CT scan. Attention shading shows model activity. Keep the predictions and highlights out of medical decisions. [Run locally](#run-locally) · [Product gallery](#product-gallery) · [Model evaluation](#model-evaluation) · [Train a model](#train-a-model) · [API](#api) ## Product gallery Every screenshot below comes from the running four-class workspace with a **real published CT image**. The screenshots demonstrate the interface. In both examples, the model predicted Normal on an image published as renal carcinoma. The class scores and overlays show what the model returned, including those errors. ### Example 1 · NIH Clinical Center CT **Image selection and preview** ![Published NIH kidney CT image preview in KidneyScan](docs/showcase/02-upload-preview.jpg) **Class scores and attention** ![Four-class output and Normal-class attention overlay for the published NIH CT](docs/showcase/03-attention-result.jpg) The model displayed **Normal** with a raw score of **80.39%**. The teal overlay corresponds to the predicted Normal class. The app’s image description reported a **301 × 306 grayscale JPEG**. **Original image comparison** ![Original NIH CT displayed alongside the same model scores](docs/showcase/04-original-comparison.jpg) **Mobile result** Source: NIH Clinical Center, serial CT example of renal cell carcinoma in von Hippel–Lindau disease. Wikimedia Commons identifies the source image as U.S. public domain. The attention view adds model-generated shading. [Image and attribution](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CT_VHL_renal.jpg). ### Example 2 · Published multiphase renal CT **Multiphase image preview** ![Uploaded multiphase renal CT figure in the desktop workspace](docs/showcase/01-multiphase-upload.jpg) **Multiphase image analysis** ![Four-class prediction and model attention for the multiphase renal CT](docs/showcase/06-multiphase-result.jpg) The model displayed **Normal** with a raw score of **90.99%** for the **793 × 226 JPEG**. This publication figure contains multiple panels, so it also illustrates the limits of feeding a composite image to a single-slice classifier. Source: Kristie Guite, Louis Hinshaw, and Fred Lee, *Computed Tomography in Abdominal Imaging: How to Gain Maximum Diagnostic Information at the Lowest Radiation Dose*. The published image is licensed [CC BY 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). The app adds attention shading in the second screenshot. [Image and attribution](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Corticomedullary_phase_CT_in_axial_and_coronal_plane,_and_parenchymal_phase,_of_renal_cell_carcinoma.jpg). ## Run locally Use Python **3.11**. From the repository root: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/DL-Kidney-CT-Classification.git cd DL-Kidney-CT-Classification python -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 python -m pip install -r requirements-demo.txt python serve.py ``` On macOS or Linux, activate the environment with `source .venv/bin/activate` before installing dependencies. Open [http://127.0.0.1:8080](http://127.0.0.1:8080), choose an image, and select **Run analysis**. The first request loads the model. | Local setup | Model used by the workspace | | --- | --- | | Fresh clone | Bundled VGG16, Normal and Tumor | | Compatible checkpoint at `artifacts/four-class-ct-cnn.keras` | Four-class CNN, Normal, Tumor, Stone, and Cyst | | Custom checkpoint path | Set `KIDNEY_FOUR_CLASS_MODEL_PATH` or `KIDNEY_MODEL_PATH` before starting the server | The app validates JPEG and PNG uploads, limits decoded files to 5 MB and 16 megapixels, and processes images in memory. The UI shows the active model. **Show original** toggles between the uploaded image and the highlight, while leaving the classification visible. The server binds to loopback by default. See the [local walkthrough](docs/DEMO.md) for setup and troubleshooting. ## Model evaluation ### Four-class CNN The four-class checkpoint reached **69.9% accuracy (1,649/2,360)** and **63.2% macro F1** on held-out filename blocks. The majority-class baseline was **41.4%**. Model selection used validation loss before scoring the test blocks. | Dataset label | Correct / tested | Recall | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Normal | 722 / 978 | 73.8% | | Tumor | 391 / 450 | 86.9% | | Stone | 87 / 265 | 32.8% | | Cyst | 449 / 667 | 67.3% | The largest errors were Normal → Tumor (184 images) and Stone → Cyst (156 images). Exact duplicates after resizing were removed and boundary slices were excluded. Verified patient identifiers were unavailable, so related slices may still cross splits. [Full evaluation and confusion matrix](docs/four-class-evaluation.json). ### Binary experiments | Evaluation | Result | Scope | | --- | ---: | --- | | Historical VGG16 validation | 48.2% | Recorded in `scores.json`. The artifact used in that run could not be tied conclusively to the bundled checkpoint. | | Bundled VGG16 on 93 held-out images | 67/93 (72.0%) | Baseline for the retrained head comparison | | Retrained VGG16 head on the same 93 images | 93/93 (100%) | Image-level split with exact duplicate grouping | | Expanded-data binary CNN | 461/465 (99.1%) | Five reused filename-block folds after pretraining on 900 screened images | The binary CNN score covers two labels on a different benchmark. The four-class app uses the separately trained four-class checkpoint. Performance on unseen patients remains unmeasured. ## Train a model Place the extracted datasets under the local `datasets/` directory. Git ignores this directory and training artifacts. | Folder | Contents and role | | --- | --- | | `datasets/CTKidney/` | The original 12,446-image archive. Folders: `normal_kidney`, `kidney_tumor`, `kidney_stone`, `cyst_kidney`. | | `datasets/Project-Kidney-CT/` | The original 465 Normal and Tumor images for the binary benchmark. | | `datasets/RenSeg-KidneyCT/` | Annotated collection kept separate. Its files overlap with the project data. | [CT Kidney dataset source](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/nazmul0087/ct-kidney-dataset-normal-cyst-tumor-and-stone) · [RenSeg-KidneyCT source](https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/rxfk6t8f6x/2) Activate the serving environment, then install scikit-learn and run one of the training commands: ```powershell python -m pip install scikit-learn # Four-class checkpoint and held-out evaluation python tools/train_four_class_cnn.py --dataset datasets/CTKidney # Binary research CNN with screened pretraining images python tools/retrain_expanded_cnn.py --export artifacts/expanded-ct-cnn-folder.keras # Binary VGG16 classifier head on the original project dataset python tools/retrain_vgg16.py ``` Four-class training saves `artifacts/four-class-ct-cnn.keras` and `artifacts/four-class-evaluation.json`. Both expanded training scripts also accept `--archive /path/to/CTKidney.zip`. Restart the server to pick up a new four-class checkpoint. The expanded-data binary CNN is a separate research artifact with a different input and output shape than the bundled VGG16 model. To run four-class inference directly in Python: ```python import numpy as np from PIL import Image, ImageOps from tensorflow.keras.models import load_model labels = ("Normal", "Tumor", "Stone", "Cyst") model = load_model("artifacts/four-class-ct-cnn.keras", compile=False) with Image.open("sample.jpg") as image: gray = ImageOps.exif_transpose(image).convert("L") prepared = ImageOps.pad(gray, (64, 64), Image.Resampling.BILINEAR, color=0) scores = model(np.asarray(prepared)[None, ..., None], training=False).numpy()[0] print(labels[scores.argmax()], dict(zip(labels, scores.tolist()))) ``` The original DVC pipeline remains available with the separate training dependencies in `requirements.txt`. It reads `config/config.yaml` and `params.yaml`, writes its model to `artifacts/training/model.h5`, and saves evaluation metrics to `scores.json`. MLflow logging is optional. ## API | Method | Endpoint | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | GET | `/` | Research workspace | | GET | `/health` | Server health and binary model load status | | GET | `/ready` | Check bundled or configured binary checkpoint readiness | | POST | `/predict` | Classify an image passed as base64 in JSON | | GET / POST | `/train` | Returns 403. Run training from the command line. | ```json { "image": "", "mode": "auto", "explain": true } ``` `auto` uses the four-class checkpoint when installed. Use `four_class` or `binary` to select explicitly. Omitting `mode` preserves the binary response. Success returns an array with the winning label in `image`, its score in `score`, all class scores in `scores`, and the serving model in `model`. With explanations enabled, the response also includes `description` and may include `attention_class` plus a base64 PNG in `attention_image`. Four-class highlights use Grad-CAM for the predicted class with input padding removed before alignment. The colors are teal for Normal, rose for Tumor, amber for Stone, and violet for Cyst. Binary VGG16 can return a Tumor-class highlight when positive evidence is available. The overlays have no verified lesion boundaries. ## Verification and deployment ```powershell python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt python -m pytest -q ``` GitHub Actions runs the test suite and a live HTTP check. The Dockerfile packages the serving environment. The AWS workflow is manual and requires infrastructure configuration. [Verification record](docs/VERIFICATION.md) · [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/vams2krish/DL-Kidney-CT-Classification/actions) ## License Project source code is under the [MIT License](LICENSE). Dataset, checkpoint, and screenshot source terms should be reviewed separately. The two published CT examples are attributed in the gallery above.

projects.name: DL-SceneTrace-3D
projects.description: Computer vision research workbench: media provenance, COLMAP camera recovery, CPU Gaussian RGB fitting, source-linked 3D review, hypothesis notes, exports, synthetic benchmarks, and a live review demo. Research baseline; not a certified forensic system.
projects.readme: # SceneTrace 3D ### Crime Scene Department · Forensic Reconstruction Unit ### Computer Vision · Gaussian Splatting · Forensic & Historical Reconstruction Research [Live review demo](https://scenetrace-3d-vams2krish.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site) · [Operations and security boundaries](docs/OPERATIONS.md) · [Dependency attribution](docs/THIRD_PARTY.md) · [Measured experiments](docs/experiments/sparse-input.json) **SceneTrace 3D turns overlapping photos or video frames into a source-linked 3D research artifact.** Inventory original media, select derivatives, estimate cameras with COLMAP, fit Gaussian colors, inspect the result in a WebGL viewer, separate observations from hypotheses, and export review records. > **Release v0.3.0: department identity and large-photo research intake.** The hosted Site is a private-to-owner static review demo. Actual media reconstruction runs through the local Python service. This is not a certified forensic tool or a production-ready multiuser service. The department emblem is an original project identity, not an insignia of an actual police agency. ## Department redesign and 128-photo live test ### Complete Capture viewpoints Capture viewpoints now lists **every selected photo**, including photographs with no recovered camera pose. Each thumbnail shows **POSE**, **NO POSE**, or **WITHHELD**. Selecting a photo always updates its source preview; camera navigation happens only when that photo has a recovered pose. Original filenames, source hashes, and per-photo roles are retained. Older scene JSON with only three registered views is expanded from its complete source manifest, so all 128 photos remain available there too. Browser-submitted reconstruction now attempts every selected photo. For a thorough local run on all downloaded photographs, use: ```powershell .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scenetrace.cli reconstruct data/crossrow/originals data/crossrow/all-128-v2 --max-frames 200 --use-all-views --thorough ``` Use a new output directory for each run. `--use-all-views` disables the earlier every-fifth-image holdout. `--thorough` uses 1600-pixel derivatives, 4096-target SIFT features, metadata-based intrinsic groups, a SIMPLE_RADIAL camera model, guided exhaustive matching, and an explicitly recorded initialization configuration. Registered views are fitted in undistorted image space. No held-out PSNR is claimed for this mode. The application now uses an original SVG shield/camera emblem, navy and evidence-gold colors, a Crime Scene Department masthead, and a forensic reconstruction desk. Large-photo intake accepts up to **200 files / 1 GiB**. Default captures over 40 training views use bounded sequential matching; thorough mode uses exhaustive matching. All registered camera poses are exported, while RGB fitting uses an explicitly recorded budget of up to 20 registered views. For the real-photo experiment, **128 original JPEGs (433,876,024 bytes, 128 distinct SHA-256 hashes)** were downloaded from [CrossRow](https://catalogue.eidf.ac.uk/dataset/eidf267-crossrow-multimodal-spatial-indoor-crime-scene-dataset), DOI [10.15132/10000293](https://doi.org/10.15132/10000293), by Vincenzo Rinaldi, Dylan Gauld, and Niamh Nic Daeid. These are genuine camera photographs of a **simulated crime scene**, not rendered images, AI-generated photographs, or evidence from an actual criminal case. Each downloaded JPEG was checked against its ZIP CRC32; individual SHA-256 values and the archive origin are recorded. The original archive is over 22 GB, so the downloader retrieves only the selected members using verified HTTP byte ranges. No copies are inserted to inflate the photo count. The [latest all-photo run](docs/experiments/crossrow-all-128.json) recovered **128 of 128 camera poses in one connected component**, with **45,985 raw sparse points / 45,928 filtered points**. It attempted all 128 photographs, withheld none, and completed in 1,040.5 seconds on the local CPU. The browser was verified with 128 selectable thumbnails, 128 registered poses, and photo 128 displaying its original filename, hash, preview, and recovered camera status. The preview contains 1,600 fixed isotropic Gaussians, with RGB fitted from 20 registered views. Training MSE decreased from 0.10717 to 0.08309, but two of three RGB solver channels reached their iteration limit (`solver_success: [true, false, false]`). Camera recovery succeeded; the appearance fit remains approximate and unconverged in those channels. No held-out accuracy, surveyed scale, or forensic validation is claimed. This is a sparse research reconstruction, not a photorealistic full-detail model. Local artifacts are in `data/crossrow/all-128-v2/`; regenerate the public numerical report with `python scripts/report_all_captures.py`. For comparison, the [first live API attempt](docs/experiments/crossrow-128-first-attempt.json) accepted all 128 files but failed COLMAP initialization. The subsequent [historical calibrated run](docs/experiments/crossrow-128.json) recovered only three poses. These earlier outcomes remain available for reproducibility. The earlier calibrated CLI rerun completed on the same original bytes with this **historical insufficient-coverage** result: | Real-photo measurement | Actual output | | --- | --- | | Original / selected photos | 128 / 128 | | SfM input / withheld photos | 102 / 26 | | Registered cameras | **3 of 102** | | Triangulated points | **39** | | Views used for Gaussian RGB fit | 3 | | Train MSE before → after | 0.23480 → 0.23299 | | Result | **Partial artifact; not a usable reconstruction of the full scene** | The live local review now loads the completed all-photo run when available, with all 128 genuine camera-photo derivatives. It falls back to the earlier artifact only when the new run is absent or incomplete. No held-out camera localization or independently surveyed geometry accuracy is claimed. The CrossRow resource is licensed **CC BY-NC-ND 4.0**. The photographs and adapted reconstruction remain in ignored local storage for noncommercial research; the public repository publishes code, attribution, original-source checksums, and numerical reports only. The hosted Site does not redistribute this scene. After a local run, open **http://127.0.0.1:8765/?dataset=crossrow** or select **Open public-photo test result**. A failed run displays its failure instead of a replacement scene. ```powershell .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/download_crossrow.py # Keep the local server running in a separate terminal. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/run_crossrow_test.py # Reuse preserved originals for a new job without uploading again: .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/run_crossrow_test.py --retry ``` **Showcase version note:** the six screenshots below document the working v0.2 interface and its synthetic experiments. They are retained as historical product captures, not represented as screenshots of the v0.3 department redesign or of the CrossRow scene. The current department identity is served by the live application. ![SceneTrace workbench running locally](docs/showcase/01-workbench.jpg) *Actual application screenshot with a procedural synthetic Gaussian room. This is not a real scene or a photorealistic reconstruction benchmark.* ## Product showcases ### Source inventory and provenance Choose local media, compute SHA-256 hashes, and submit explicitly to the local worker. Originals remain separate from selected image derivatives. ![Local media inventory with real calculated source hashes](docs/showcase/04-source-inventory.jpg) ### Validation with held-out comparisons Inspect the synthetic observation and fitted Gaussian render side by side, read the actual metrics, and keep evaluation caveats visible. ![Held-out appearance comparison and limitations](docs/showcase/02-validation.jpg) ### Separate observation and hypothesis layers Notes reference specific source views and persist per scene in browser storage. Both layers are included in the review JSON export. ![Observation and hypothesis notes in the running product](docs/showcase/03-review-notes.jpg) ### Actual browser-to-COLMAP output The browser uploaded nine synthetic textured captures, the local worker recovered cameras and sparse geometry, fitted Gaussian colors, and returned this navigable artifact. The sparse appearance is an actual output limitation, not concealed by substituting the synthetic room. ![Completed local COLMAP reconstruction from browser-submitted captures](docs/showcase/05-colmap-result.jpg) ### Responsive review All showcase images above are screenshots of the running product. The [original AI-generated concept banner](docs/assets/scenetrace-concept.png) is retained separately with its [prompt and disclosure](docs/illustration-prompt.md); it is not a product result. Browser/Windows screenshot automation could not initialize during the department redesign, so fresh v0.3 screenshots and visual QA are not claimed. The HTTP-served HTML/logo and static JavaScript checks were verified; the historical gallery is explicitly labeled v0.2. ## What works today | Capability | Implemented behavior | | --- | --- | | Source inventory | SHA-256, source-byte counts, stable source IDs, decode failure records | | Frame preparation | JPEG/PNG/WebP; OpenCV video extraction; interval and candidate budget; normalized PNG derivatives | | Selection decisions | Laplacian sharpness heuristic and exact normalized-pixel duplicate detection, recorded per candidate | | Camera recovery | CPU PyCOLMAP feature extraction, exhaustive matching, incremental mapping, camera export | | Gaussian reconstruction | Original CPU backend with fixed isotropic geometry/scales/opacity and bounded least-squares RGB fitting | | Synthetic evaluation | Seeded 1,789-Gaussian room, six training views and two held-out views, PSNR and train MSE | | Review UI | Orbit/zoom, point mode, camera navigation, source hashes, validation comparisons, responsive layout | | Review notes | Source-linked observations and hypotheses; scene-specific browser persistence; removal and export | | Local job service | One active subprocess, thirty-minute deadline, persisted success/failure, preserved-original retry, review ZIP export | | Hosted demo | Static deployment with committed synthetic artifacts, local hashing, JSON import, notes and exports | | Verification | Automated integrity/API tests, v0.2 live browser flow, 128-real-photo intake, preserved failure and insufficient-coverage reports, CI workflow | ## Run the demo locally Use **Python 3.12** for the tested environment. No OpenAI key, external AI API, GPU, COLMAP executable, Node dependency installation, or FFmpeg executable is required. PyCOLMAP and OpenCV wheels supply the used functionality. ```powershell git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/DL-SceneTrace-3D.git cd DL-SceneTrace-3D python -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-lock.txt .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --no-deps -e . .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scenetrace.cli serve ``` Open **http://127.0.0.1:8765/**. On Linux/macOS, replace `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe` with `.venv/bin/python`. 1. Explore the synthetic room, select source thumbnails, and compare held-out views in **Validation**. 2. Add an observation and a hypothesis in **Review notes**, reload, and export the review JSON. 3. In **Source inventory**, choose 4–200 overlapping photos or a video. Up to 200 files and 1 GiB of source bytes are accepted by the local UI. 4. Submit **Run local reconstruction**. The worker requires at least four distinct, sufficiently sharp derivative views. Registration can fail when overlap or texture is inadequate. 5. Inspect the returned scene, source records, and limitations. Download the worker review bundle. Failed jobs expose their reason instead of substituting a demo scene. The hosted Site runs the review functions without a Python server. Its reconstruction control remains unavailable; it does not upload files or run COLMAP in the cloud. Scene JSON can be imported there, but its relative source-image links require the local service or a corresponding artifact directory; imported JSON does not embed source media. This release accepts its own schema, not arbitrary `.ply` or `.splat` files. ## Reproduce the complete synthetic photo pipeline ```powershell # Make perspective photographs of textured synthetic 3D patches. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/generate_sfm_fixture.py data/sfm-input # Inventory only, with explicit derivative selection parameters. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scenetrace.cli inventory data/sfm-input data/inventory-run --max-frames 40 # Recover cameras and geometry from pixels, then fit Gaussian RGB. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scenetrace.cli reconstruct data/sfm-input data/reconstruction-run # Independently regenerate the supplied-camera appearance-fitting demo. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scenetrace.cli demo data/gaussian-demo-run # Controlled 4/6/9-view experiment; work directory must be new. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/sparse_experiment.py --work data/experiment-new # With the local server running: verify a real subprocess failure and queue release. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/verify_local_api.py .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q ``` Outputs are never silently overwritten by the inventory/reconstruction commands; choose a new output directory for reruns. The Gaussian demo command regenerates its explicitly selected demo destination. CLI inventory supports `--interval` in seconds and `--max-frames` (candidate budget, including rejected candidates). ## Measured output ### Gaussian optimizer experiment | Measurement | Observed result | | --- | --- | | Scene | Procedural archive room; seed 17 | | Gaussians | 1,789 | | Training / held-out views | 6 / 2 | | Training MSE before → after | 0.00379316 → 0.00000158 | | Mean held-out PSNR | 56.61 dB | | RGB solver success | All three channels | See [committed metrics](demo/dist/sample/metrics.json), [scene artifact](demo/dist/sample/scene.json), and [generator](scenetrace/demo.py). **Interpretation:** cameras, geometry, scale, and opacity are supplied by the synthetic generator. Only colors are fitted. The same renderer generates and evaluates observations; the score is an optimizer smoke test and does not predict real-scene reconstruction quality. ### Camera recovery from rendered photographs (v0.2 baseline) These experiments use a separate seed-21 textured 3D-patch fixture. Camera poses are estimated from the image pixels through COLMAP; ground-truth poses are not passed to reconstruction. | Input captures | Cameras registered | Triangulated points | Train MSE after RGB fit | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4 | 4 | 4,934 | 0.04153 | | 6 | 6 | 7,444 | 0.03261 | | 9 | 7 | 8,521 | 0.02922 | The nine-view run excludes two images from both SfM and fitting. Independent localization of those held-out images is not implemented, so no held-out score is claimed for these reconstructions. Four/six-view runs use all selected views. The [full report](docs/experiments/sparse-input.json) includes runtime and similarity-aligned camera-center diagnostics. Alignment is fitted to the same training camera centers; it is not independent geometry validation. Timings depend on the host and are not throughput claims. A separate live browser run also registered seven cameras from nine uploaded synthetic images and produced a downloadable worker bundle. [Live duplicate-media failure report](docs/experiments/api-failure.json) verifies that inadequate distinct views fail explicitly and release the worker slot. ## How reconstruction works ```mermaid fl

projects.readme: # SignBridge — ISL Learning & Accessibility Studio **Indian Sign Language learning · Personal pose vocabulary · Gesture → speech · Saved-pose previews** A working ISL-focused learning workspace with on-device deep learning, editable captions, personal static-pose learning, and a 3D companion named Ari. **[Open the live demo](https://signbridge-gesture-lab.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site)** · Hosted privately through Sites; sign in with the owning account. The source repository remains public. > **Release scope:** deployable research demo, not a production-ready sign-language interpreter. This version combines **7 built-in demo gestures**, **207 searchable practice prompts**, and **up to 200 user-taught static poses**. Practice prompts are not pretrained recognition classes. It does not translate ISL sentences, continuous signing, or arbitrary text. No translation-accuracy claim is made. ## Product showcases These are actual screenshots of the implemented application. The original AI-generated cover remains in [concept artwork](docs/artwork.md). ### 1. The studio Permission-based camera input, local vision, editable captions, speech controls, and a 3D avatar in one workspace. ![SignBridge studio with camera controls, captions, avatar and seven-gesture library](docs/showcase/01-studio.png) ### 2. Real model recognition The sample button runs the actual MediaPipe model on an attributed test photograph. A thumb-up classification proposes “Yes” for review. The confidence shown is a model score, not measured accuracy; the inference time is specific to the test device and excludes capture, holding, review, and speech. ![Actual thumb-up sample recognition with landmarks, model score and editable Yes caption](docs/showcase/02-recognition.png) ### 3. Text to avatar “Peace” selects the illustrative Victory pose. The avatar has articulated fingers, a procedural upper body, adjustable idle motion, and decorative mouth movement during speech. These motions are not linguist-validated sign-language animations. ![Speech and text input driving the Victory gesture on the Ari avatar](docs/showcase/03-avatar.png) ### 4. ISL learning and the gesture library Search 207 categorized practice prompts, open the official ISLRTC dictionary, and send a prompt into the personal teacher. The seven built-in categories remain separately labeled as generic demo gestures. ![ISL practice catalog with official dictionary link, search, and built-in demo gestures](docs/showcase/04-library.png) ### 5. Mobile layout The studio stacks its input and output panels on smaller screens, with the same consent, fallback, and caption controls. Browser support for camera, speech recognition, and WebGL varies; physical mobile-device validation remains pending. ### 6. Teach a personal vocabulary Capture 12–24 examples of a distinct static pose, label it, test it, and deliberately export/import your vocabulary. No photographs are saved. The showcase below maps a sample thumb pose to an arbitrary test phrase; **it does not demonstrate the ISL sign for water**. ![Personal gesture teacher with capture controls, saved phrase, and vocabulary export and import](docs/showcase/06-personal-learning.png) ### 7. Preview your own saved hand landmarks A matching text phrase can display your captured static pose instead of inventing an unfamiliar signing motion. This is a landmark preview, not a validated signing avatar or movement reconstruction. ![User-taught phrase displaying saved personal hand landmarks](docs/showcase/07-saved-pose.png) ## What works now | Capability | Implementation and boundary | | --- | --- | | Live gesture recognition | Self-hosted MediaPipe VIDEO tracking in a worker, hardware GPU/CPU selection, one- or two-hand capture | | Temporal proposal filtering | Default 70% threshold, 350 ms/three-result hold, 150 ms dropout tolerance; labeled low-confidence assist after a longer hold | | Sample without camera | Real inference on Google's attributed thumb-up test photo; no synthetic prediction | | ISL practice library | 207 organized prompts linked to the official dictionary; not pretrained recognition classes | | Personal static-pose learner | 12–24 examples per pose, up to 200 labels, distance/ambiguity rejection, export/import | | Responsiveness diagnostics | Tracked hands, lighting/framing hints, processing FPS, rolling inference p95, resolution/hold/backend controls | | Caption review | Editable/appendable caption, user-triggered speech, stop speaking, voice selection | | Speech input | Optional browser speech recognition with separate consent and editable transcript | | Text/speech to avatar | Whole-phrase matching against built-in intents or personal captions; personal matches show saved landmarks, unsupported text remains visible | | Avatar | Procedural Three.js character with articulated fingers and seven illustrative static gesture poses | | Privacy controls | No application recording, upload, analytics, backend, or persistent conversation storage | | Session history | Confirmed speech and avatar messages in memory, capped at 20; clear session also stops devices | | Accessibility | Semantic controls, native modal dialogs, visible focus, live status, reduced-motion option, text fallback | | Evaluation tooling | Local image-manifest harness with declared signer separation, duplicate detection, confusion matrix and latency | | Verification | Unit tests, browser integration tests, accessibility scan, production build, dependency audit, GitHub Actions workflow | Browser speech recognition may send audio to its provider. TTS voices can be local or remote; local voices are labeled. Camera processing stays on the device. Hiding the page, switching the app view/direction, or clearing the session stops active capture and speech. ## Is it ML, DL, or GenAI? **Classification: hybrid Deep Learning + Machine Learning (DL + ML).** Pretrained MediaPipe neural networks supply visual perception; a nearest-neighbor ML matcher learns personal static-pose examples. Temporal confidence filtering and phrase mapping are deterministic application logic. The avatar is procedural animation. There is no LLM, generative translation model, or OpenAI API dependency. The long-term project remains **Deep Learning — SignBridge Accessibility Agent**, with ISL–English translation as the chosen future research direction. ISL dialect and use-case scope must be agreed with Deaf collaborators and sign-language specialists; seven hand categories do not establish support for a natural sign language. ## Try it locally Requirements: **Node.js 24**, npm, an internet connection for the initial dependency/model download, and a current desktop Chromium browser. Camera access requires HTTPS or localhost. Text input and captions remain available if optional speech APIs are unsupported. ```bash git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/DL-SignBridge.git cd DL-SignBridge/app npm ci npm run assets npm run dev ``` Open the Local URL printed by Vite, normally `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`. No API key or account database is needed. Model and WASM assets are self-hosted after preparation; there is no service-worker/offline-install guarantee. ### Walk through both directions 1. Choose **Run sample photo**. Wait for the real model to propose **Yes**. 2. Edit the caption if needed, then choose **Speak caption**. Choose an installed voice under **Studio settings** if necessary. 3. To use a camera, choose **Enable camera**, review consent, then grant browser permission. Hold one supported gesture steady until a proposal appears. Review before speaking. 4. Switch to **Speech / text → Avatar**. Type **Peace** or select a phrase and choose **Animate message**. 5. Optionally choose **Use microphone**, review its separate privacy notice, dictate a supported phrase, and review the transcript before animating it. 6. Try an unsupported sentence: the app preserves the text and declines to invent a gesture. 7. Use **Clear session & stop devices** to stop camera, microphone, and speech and clear session content. ## Personal ISL learning and latency improvements 1. Open **Gesture library**, search a practice prompt, and consult the **official ISL dictionary** with a qualified signer. 2. Choose **Teach this pose**. In Studio settings, select one or two hands, then enable the camera. 3. Enter a distinct name and caption. Capture examples, save, release the pose, and test again in **Personal recognition** mode. 4. Review the proposed caption before speech. Use the exact saved caption in text mode to preview its stored hand landmarks. 5. Export deliberately before reloading; the vocabulary otherwise stays in this tab. Landmark files are personal data even without photos. A static learner cannot model ISL movement, face/body grammar, or signs distinguished only by location on the body. Similar handshapes may be rejected or confused. The 200-pose limit is capacity, not a count of independently validated signs. VIDEO tracking reduced warm median inference from **75.9 ms to 48.6 ms** (about 36%) in a controlled repeated-photo, one-hand CPU comparison. First-frame VIDEO inference was slower. This is not a promised end-to-end latency improvement. See [measurement and tradeoffs](docs/latency.md), [raw benchmark](docs/performance-tracking.json), and [personal-learning details](docs/isl-personal-learning.md). Built-in **assist mode** explicitly permits a stable score up to eight percentage points below the chosen threshold after at least one second and six matching results. Proposals are labeled and require review. Turn it off for stricter abstention. It does not apply to personal matching. Physical camera validation was attempted on this execution host but was unavailable; generated camera-stream tests exercise actual neural inference and track cleanup. ## Supported demo vocabulary | Model category | Demo phrase | Reverse-input aliases | | --- | --- | --- | | `Open_Palm` | Hello | hello, hi, open palm | | `Thumb_Up` | Yes | yes, thumb up, thumbs up | | `Thumb_Down` | No | no, thumb down, thumbs down | | `Closed_Fist` | Wait | wait, fist, closed fist | | `Pointing_Up` | One moment | one moment, point up, pointing up | | `Victory` | Peace | peace, victory | | `ILoveYou` | I love you | i love you | Matching is case-insensitive and ignores common punctuation; it requires the complete supported phrase. For example, “No thanks” is unsupported even though “No” is supported. Manual library previews are explicitly labeled and do not create camera-recognition results. ## Current architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD Camera[User-authorized camera] --> Frames[One in-flight image bitmap] Sample[Attributed sample photo] --> Worker Frames --> Worker[Browser worker: MediaPipe neural inference] Assets[Self-hosted model and WASM] --> Worker Worker --> Landmarks[Gesture category, landmarks and timing] Landmarks --> Gate[Category allowlist, confidence and camera hold] Gate --> Review[Editable caption proposal] Review --> Confirm[User chooses Speak caption] Confirm --> TTS[Browser text-to-speech] TTS --> Speaking[Decorative avatar mouth animation] Mic[Separately consented microphone] --> ASR[Optional browser speech provider] ASR --> Text[Editable English text] Typed[Typed phrase] --> Text Text --> Exact[Whole-phrase vocabulary matching] Exact --> Supported[Supported illustrative pose] Exact --> Fallback[Unsupported: visible text fallback] Supported --> Avatar[Three.js procedural avatar] ``` The model runs off the UI thread. Camera frames preserve their source aspect ratio for inference, with letterboxed preview and landmark alignment. Media tracks, worker resources, and avatar GPU resources have explicit cleanup paths. The 3D renderer loads separately from the initial interface bundle. ## Verify and build From `app/`: ```bash npm test npm run build npm audit --audit-level=moderate npx playwright install chromium npm run test:e2e npm run preview ``` Browser tests run against a dedicated local production-preview port. The sample test uses actual model inference. Physical audio output and microphone recognition are stubbed at their browser API boundaries in automated tests. A generated camera stream from the attributed sample exercises the actual frame loop and hold gate; this does not validate a physical camera or a real signer's performance. The test suite regenerates the README's seven showcases. Dependency licenses and model provenance are documented in [third-party notices](app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [the model provenance manifest](app/public/models/provenance.json). See [evaluation protocol](docs/evaluation.md) for a private dataset harness and [production readiness](docs/production-readiness.md) for the remaining release gates. The GitHub workflow runs install, asset preparation, tests, build, audit, and browser checks on pushes and pull requests. Latest local verification: **32 unit tests and 8 browser tests passed**, production build passed, no violations in the tested initial accessibility scan, and zero known dependency vulnerabilities. Read the [verification report](docs/verification.md) for the exact tested boundaries and limitations. The original demo was published on October 28, 2026; this revision adds the ISL personal-learning workflow. ## Roadmap and honest progress - [x] Build a responsive studio with camera permission, caption review, avatar controls, and text fallback. - [x] Integrate a pretrained seven-category gesture baseline and real-model functional sample. - [x] Filter camera proposals by confidence, hold time, and release before repeating. - [x] Connect reviewed captions to speech and a bounded speech/text-to-avatar pathway. - [x] Add a gesture library, privacy notices, session clearing, and reduced decorative motion. - [x] Add reproducible evaluation tooling, automated checks, CI, and actual product screenshots. - [x] Prioritize ISL learning, add 207 practice prompts, and link official ISLRTC references. - [x] Add up to 200 personal static poses, one/two-hand features, capture/export/import, rejection, and saved-pose previews. - [x] Add video tracking, labeled low-confidence assist, performance controls, and camera diagnostics. - [ ] Validate ISL dialect, use cases, and forms with compensated Deaf collaborators. - [ ] Establish a consented, representative, signer-disjoint evaluation dataset and publish metrics. - [ ] Train or integrate language-specific recognition and translation models, including continuous signing and non-manual grammar. - [ ] Add linguist-reviewed motion clips and validate avatar comprehensibility with fluent signers. - [ ] Measure end-to-end conversational latency on named physical devices and browsers. - [ ] Complete physical hardware, assistive-technology, independent accessibility, security, and operational release reviews. - [ ] Explore constrained generative motion only after validated baselines exist. The completed baseline is gesture classification and personal static-pose matching, not completion of the ISL translation research goals. A successful test photograph does not establish generalization or translation accuracy. This demo should not be used as a substitute for a qualified interpreter in critical interactions. ## Repository layout ```text DL-SignBridge/ ├── app/ │ ├── src/ # React studio, camera/speech hooks, domain logic, avatar │ ├── public/ # Worker, sample photo, generated local model/WASM assets │ ├── scripts/ # Asset preparation, local model diagnostics, evaluation │ ├── tests/ # Browser integration and accessibility tests │ ├── .openai/hosting.json # Sites identity and static hosting configuration │ └── THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md ├── docs/ │ ├── showcase/

projects.readme: # DL – SugarLens **Private, on-device produce recognition with transparent sugar estimates. Web, mobile PWA, and Capacitor native packaging.** [Open the live demo](https://sugarlens-produce-vams2krish.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site) · [Source code](https://github.com/vams2krish/DL-SugarLens) · [Model and data limitations](#scope-and-limitations) The live deployment retains owner-only access; the GitHub source is public. Sign in with the owner's account to open the hosted app. ![SugarLens product overview: scanner, food insights, portion list and food library](docs/showcase-desktop.png) SugarLens identifies supported fruits and vegetables from a photo or local live camera feed, asks you to confirm the match, and looks up average natural sugar content from USDA FoodData Central. It never claims to measure sugar or portion weight from pixels. The produce-market redesign uses a leafy green, oat and citrus palette, with camera access first and a separate sugar profile. Version 1.2 adds an explicit webcam/mobile camera workspace, photo capture and live recognition alongside the 28-food library, portion comparisons, CSV export, offline models and native packaging commands. ## Camera and live video — version 1.2 The earlier **Take a photo** button was a file chooser with `capture="environment"`. That hint can open the system camera on a phone, but it does not implement a desktop webcam preview or continuous video recognition. Version 1.2 uses the browser's **getUserMedia** API to request a local video stream explicitly. 1. Open the HTTPS live app in a supported browser and click **Open camera**. 2. Allow **Camera** when the browser asks. No microphone access is requested. 3. Choose **Default / rear camera**, **Front camera**, or a named connected camera. 4. Click **Capture photo** to freeze and analyze one frame. The camera turns off after capture. 5. Or click **Start live scanning**. Recognition runs serially on resized frames, with a 700 ms minimum gap after each inference; the rate depends on your device. Multiple-items mode draws detection boxes. 6. **Pause scanning** keeps the preview on without inference. **Stop camera** releases every video track. 7. Choose **Freeze & confirm** on a live suggestion to stop the camera, freeze the analyzed frame and show the food's reference sugar profile. Enter its weighed edible portion before adding it to your list. This is **local live video preview and recognition**, not a broadcast, recorded clip or remote video call. Video frames are not uploaded, saved in scan history or sent to an AI server. The camera stops when the page is hidden, the user leaves it, or the device disconnects. ### Webcam preview ![Camera workspace with a running virtual webcam preview](docs/showcase-camera-preview.png) ### Capture a frame and calculate sugar ![Camera capture recognized by MobileNet with a 200 g banana portion](docs/showcase-camera-capture.png) ### Continuous live recognition ![Live camera classification with a freeze-and-confirm action](docs/showcase-live-scanning.png) ### Live object detection ![Real COCO-SSD detection on video frames with an overlay](docs/showcase-live-detection.png) ### Camera on a phone-sized screen ### Helpful recovery when the host blocks camera access ![Camera permission-policy recovery with external-browser and upload guidance](docs/showcase-camera-recovery.png) **Showcase provenance:** these camera screenshots use a Chromium virtual webcam fed with the licensed banana photograph. They exercise actual `getUserMedia`, video-to-canvas capture and the real neural networks. They are not evidence of physical webcam or iPhone/Android hardware certification. No personal camera footage is published to this repository. ### If your camera does not open | Symptom | What to check | | --- | --- | | No live camera API | Use current Chrome, Edge or Safari over HTTPS; some embedded browsers do not expose camera access | | Permission denied | Allow Camera in the browser's site settings and OS privacy settings, then retry | | Camera blocked by page policy | Open the HTTPS app in a standalone browser; an embedded frame cannot override its parent's camera policy | | No camera found | Connect a webcam or use a phone; uploads and manual lookup remain available | | Camera busy | Close other apps using it, then reopen the camera | | Wrong camera | Choose a named camera or Front/Default source; camera availability depends on the device | | Live model cannot load | Check the connection, or download the recognition models before going offline | **Use phone camera** retains the native file-capture fallback. Uploading an existing photo works even when live camera access is unavailable. Live capture needs HTTPS or localhost, an available device, and browser/OS permission. See [getUserMedia requirements](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia) and [camera permissions policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Permissions-Policy/camera). ## Product showcases ### 1. Real photo → confirmation → sugar estimate The **Try a real photo demo** button runs the actual MobileNet model on the included banana photograph. After confirmation, entering 200 g produces an estimate of **24.40 g sugar**. No recognition responses are mocked or prerecorded. ![Actual banana photo recognition and reference sugar profile](docs/showcase-photo-scan.png) ### 2. More than one item in a photo COCO-SSD locates supported objects independently and draws numbered bounding boxes. Each match has its own confirmation button. This showcase uses two copies of the licensed demo photograph, with two real detections. ![Multi-item recognition with two separately detected bananas](docs/showcase-multiple-items.png) ### 3. Compare real portions and export your list Add a weighed portion of each confirmed food. A 200 g banana portion plus 100 g strawberry contains approximately **29.29 g total sugar** in 300 g food, or **9.76% by mass**. The total is a mass-weighted calculation, not a sum of food percentages. Download the actual rows as a CSV. ![Portion comparison with total grams, sugar and weighted percentage](docs/showcase-portions.png) ### 4. Save recognition for offline use Download both model weights to browser IndexedDB, check their saved status, or remove them. The production service worker precaches app code, bundled fonts, the food library and demo photo. Recognition loads the saved weights after a reload without contacting an inference server. ![Offline model download, check and removal controls](docs/showcase-offline.png) ### 5. The mobile experience The same features adapt to a narrow phone viewport. Camera capture and photo selection are separate controls. Add the PWA to your home screen through the browser menu. ## Is this ML, DL or Gen AI? **Deep Learning (DL), a subset of Machine Learning (ML).** MobileNet V2 performs single-image classification; COCO-SSD with a Lite MobileNet V2 backbone performs object detection. These are pretrained neural networks running through TensorFlow.js in the browser. This project uses inference, not a newly trained produce-specific model. It is not generative AI. Sugar estimates come from reviewed nutrition records and arithmetic. ## What shipped in version 1.1 | Roadmap area | Delivered behavior | | --- | --- | | Multiple foods | Numbered bounding boxes and independent confirmation for supported COCO-SSD produce classes | | Nutrition coverage | 28 raw produce records, each matched against saved USDA API snapshots | | Exploration | Search by food name, sort by sugar/name, show all/fewer foods | | Portion comparisons | Add/remove up to 100 portions, mass-weighted total, tab-session recovery and CSV export | | Offline recognition | Explicit model download, check and removal using versioned IndexedDB entries | | Offline app | Versioned service worker precache, local fonts, update prompt and offline connection indicator | | Product demo | Bundled, licensed real photograph; real inference; reproducible two-object E2E fixture | | Native delivery | Capacitor config plus reproducible Android/iOS preparation commands; Android generation/sync verified | | Verification | Unit tests, production-browser E2E checks, mobile layout and real-model inference checks | ## Run locally Use **Node.js 22.12+** and npm (Capacitor CLI requires Node 22+). ```bash npm ci npm run dev ``` For a production demo on your computer: ```bash npm run build npm run preview -- --port 4173 ``` Open `http://127.0.0.1:4173`. The first online visit precaches the shell. Click **Download models** before trying offline recognition. On a phone, open the HTTPS deployment; your computer's loopback URL does not point to the computer from another device. ## Repeatable end-to-end demo 1. Click **Try a real photo demo**. Wait for real inference, then confirm **Banana**. 2. Enter **200** in edible portion grams. Verify **24.40 g sugar**, then **Add portion to list**. 3. Choose **Strawberry**, leave 100 g, and add it. Verify the total **29.29 g sugar / 9.76%**. 4. Click **Download CSV** and inspect the two source-linked rows. 5. Select **Multiple items**, then **Scan in selected mode**. The detector draws a banana box. Upload your own photo containing supported objects to explore multiple matches. 6. Search **blue** in the library and select **Blueberry** for its USDA sugar profile. 7. Click **Download models**, wait until both say **yes**, reload, and check their status. 8. Disable network access and reload. Repeat the photo demo in both modes; manual food lookup and portions also remain available. 9. Remove saved models. Without network access, recognition explains the missing download while manual lookup continues working. Actual photographed food can be misidentified. Confirm every match and correct it manually before relying on reference values. ## Recognition and nutrition coverage **Single-produce mode:** ImageNet labels for Granny Smith/apple, banana, orange, strawberry, pineapple, lemon, broccoli, cucumber, cauliflower, bell pepper, zucchini/courgette and head cabbage. Suggestions require at least 10% model probability. The general apple reference is not variety-specific; bell pepper uses the red sweet pepper reference. **Multi-item mode:** apple, banana, orange, broccoli and carrot only, with a 50% score threshold and up to 20 objects per image. Other COCO classes are ignored. Detection boxes do not measure edible mass, reliably count obscured fruit, or segment the food. Thresholds are usability filters, not calibrated accuracy guarantees. **Manual library:** Apple, Banana, Orange, Strawberry, Pineapple, Lemon, Broccoli, Cucumber, Carrot, Tomato, Watermelon, Grapes, Avocado, Cauliflower, Red bell pepper, Zucchini, Cabbage, Mango, Blueberry, Raspberry, Pear, Peach, Plum, Kiwi, Spinach, Celery, Onion and Potato. Every record links to its USDA FDC ID. Reviewed snapshots are in [`docs/usda-reference-snapshot.json`](docs/usda-reference-snapshot.json) and [`docs/usda-roadmap-snapshot.json`](docs/usda-roadmap-snapshot.json), retrieved October 28, 2026. Tests assert that all bundled sugar values match these snapshots. ```text Photo → local MobileNet classification / COCO-SSD detection → user confirmation → USDA reference → user-entered edible grams → estimated sugar → optional portion list and CSV Food sugar % by mass = grams total sugar per 100 g food Portion sugar = food sugar per 100 g × edible portion grams ÷ 100 Combined sugar % = sum(portion sugar) ÷ sum(portion grams) × 100 ``` ## Offline use, privacy and updates The production build precaches its versioned app shell, JavaScript modules, local fonts, demo image and source-backed food table. Model weights are saved only after **Download models**. This uses roughly 40 MB for models plus app resources, depending on backend/version. Browser storage limits, private browsing and automatic eviction can prevent persistence. **Check saved models** before travelling; download success does not guarantee indefinite storage retention. Uploaded photos are decoded into an in-memory canvas, resized to a maximum 1,280 px edge for inference, and never uploaded or persisted. Inputs are limited to JPG/PNG/WebP, 12 MB, and 40 megapixels. Convert unsupported formats such as HEIC first. New or invalid uploads clear previous photo results. The portion list stores only food IDs and entered weights in `sessionStorage`; clear it explicitly or close the tab. No account database, photo history or analytics is included. Initial model downloads use TensorFlow/Google model hosting, which receives ordinary network metadata. Font files are bundled locally. Online navigation refreshes through the host so its authentication redirects remain valid; offline navigation reconstructs the saved shell response without redirect or compression metadata. A dedicated service-worker regression test covers this hosted reload path. New app versions show an update action; activating it preserves the current tab's portion list. Model removal clears the saved recognition weights without deleting food data or the app shell. ## Mobile and native packaging The deployed version is an **installable PWA**, not a signed app-store binary. iPhone Safari: **Share → Add to Home Screen**. Android Chrome: **Install app / Add to Home screen**. The in-app install button opens the browser install prompt where available, otherwise it displays instructions. Capacitor packaging shares the production `dist/` implementation: ```bash npm run native:android npx cap open android # Run on a Mac with Xcode for iOS development npm run native:ios npx cap open ios ``` The preparation commands create the platform folder if needed and sync the current web build. Generated platform folders are ignored so they can be recreated. Android source generation and sync were verified on Windows. Building/signing Android requires Android Studio and the Android SDK; iOS builds/signing require macOS and Xcode. Camera chooser behavior and offline storage must be validated on physical target devices before store submission. No APK, AAB, IPA or store release is claimed in this version. Native preparation also adds the Android `CAMERA` manifest permission (with optional camera hardware) or the iOS `NSCameraUsageDescription` purpose text. It does not add microphone permission. Runtime camera prompts still require the user's approval; these source settings are not a substitute for native-device testing. ## Verification and delivery ```bash npm test npm run build npm run preview -- --port 4173 # Keep running in a separate terminal npm run test:e2e npm run test:camera ``` E2E uses local Microsoft Edge through Playwright. In CI it uses Playwright Chromium (`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`). It tests the actual production build and real models, not mocked predictions. It covers photo confirmation, two-object detection, portion arithmetic and CSV bytes, nutrition search, offline model persistence/reload, invalid image recovery, mobile overflow, removal and missing-model fallback. It also captures the README showcases and writes an inspectable result to [`docs/verification.json`](docs/verification.json). The automated demo is a small curated regression test, not a statistically meaningful accuracy benchmark. It cannot replace diverse camera testing, accessibility review or physical-device validation. Dependency audits check known advisories at the time they run; they are not a security certification. The camera suite generates an ignored Y4M test video from the bundled, licensed banana photo and supplies it through

projects.name: FartAlert
projects.description: A playful Electron desktop app that detects system-wide inactivity and plays random fart sounds until you return. Features three sound themes, custom WAV/MP3 uploads that activate instantly, adjustable idle timeout, frequency and volume, animated cloud particles, and local-only storage. Built with React, Vite, Web Audio and Framer Motion.
projects.readme:
# 💨 Fart Alert

### Step away. Let it rip.

A playful desktop app that turns computer inactivity into a questionable soundtrack. Fart Alert detects system-wide mouse and keyboard inactivity, plays random fart sounds when you step away, and stops playback when you return.

Built with **Electron, React, Vite, Web Audio, and Framer Motion**. Settings and custom sounds stay on your device.

**[Try the live browser demo on Vercel](https://fartalert.vercel.app/)** · **[Run the Windows desktop edition](#quick-start)**

The browser demo monitors activity inside its own page. The Windows app uses the operating system idle timer for desktop-wide detection.

## Product showcase

Screenshots from the production demo: midnight surfaces, mint controls, violet monitoring states, and a responsive layout.

### Ready for a little chaos

The main dashboard starts paused, with clear controls for activation, sound previews, and your inactivity threshold.

![Dashboard paused and ready to activate](docs/images/01-ready.png)

### Musical Farts and particle bursts

Choose a sound personality and preview it. The cloud mascot reacts while colorful particles burst during playback.

![Musical Farts preview with animated cloud and colorful particles](docs/images/02-musical-burst.png)

### Bring your own sounds

Uploaded sounds enable immediately. Each file has its own preview, enable toggle, and delete control. Here, Bubble-trouble is enabled and Rumble-remix is saved but disabled.

![Custom WAV sound library with one enabled and one disabled sound](docs/images/03-custom-library.png)

### Step away: automatic playback

The browser demo plays the enabled custom WAV after five seconds of real inactivity in the page.

![Browser demo playing custom audio after the idle timer expires](docs/images/04-idle-playing.png)

### Come back: quiet again

Input resets the idle timer and stops automatic playback. Monitoring stays armed for the next time you step away.

![Browser demo returned to its active monitoring state](docs/images/05-returned-active.png)

### Mobile browser layout

The settings and monitor stack on narrow screens. See the [390 px mobile screenshot](docs/images/06-mobile.png).

### Native Windows playback

![Packaged Windows app playing custom audio after the operating-system idle timer triggers](docs/images/04-native-idle-playing.png)

The [Windows return-to-active capture](docs/images/07-native-returned.png) shows the monitor after system activity stopped playback.

## Features

- **System-wide inactivity detection:** mouse and keyboard activity anywhere on your computer resets the idle timer, including while the app is minimized.
- **Automatic playback and stop:** repeat random sounds while idle; stop when activity resumes. Activity is checked approximately every 250 ms.
- **Configurable timeout:** 5 seconds to 2 minutes, with a 10-second default.
- **Three sound themes:** Cartoon Chaos, Heavy Duty, and Musical Farts.
- **Frequency and volume controls:** Gentle, Standard, or Extreme, plus a sound test button.
- **Custom WAV/MP3 uploads:** preview, enable, disable, and delete individual sounds.
- **Playful visuals:** animated cloud mascot, colorful particle bursts, idle progress, and a session fart counter.
- **Local persistence:** settings and uploaded sounds survive restarts. Monitoring starts paused on every launch.

## Quick start

### Requirements

- Node.js **22.12 or later** and npm; initially built and tested with Node.js 24.
- Windows for the included portable packaging script and desktop test setup.
- An audio output device with its volume turned up.
- Internet access for the initial dependency and Electron runtime downloads.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/FartAlert.git
cd FartAlert
npm ci
npm run build
npm start
```

1. Click **Test sound** to check your audio.
2. Choose your timeout, sound personality, frequency, and volume.
3. Click **Activate Fart Alert**.
4. Stop using the mouse and keyboard and wait for the timeout.
5. Move the mouse or press a key to stop the idle playback.

Click **Pause Fart Alert** to disable monitoring. Minimizing the window keeps monitoring active; closing it quits the app. The app does not prevent sleep, so sleeping the computer suspends it.

## Custom sounds: upload → active → idle playback

**Uploading a valid sound automatically enables it.** No second selection is needed.

Choose one or more `.wav` or `.mp3` files in **Your secret weapons**. Each file must be **15 MB or less** and successfully decode as audio. Accepted files appear with their enabled toggle checked.

| Control or state | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Play icon beside a file | Preview that specific sound |
| Checked toggle | Include the file in random idle playback |
| Disabled toggle | Keep the file saved but exclude it from idle playback |
| Trash icon | Remove the saved sound |
| One or more custom sounds enabled | Randomly choose from those files instead of the built-in theme |
| All custom sounds disabled | Use the selected built-in theme again |

Random selection can repeat the same file. Previewing a file does not change its enabled state. Uploading a sound does not activate monitoring if monitoring is paused.

Files are stored locally in IndexedDB. There is no server upload, account requirement, or cloud synchronization. Clearing the app's local data removes saved files and settings.

## Sound themes and frequency

| Theme | Personality |
| --- | --- |
| Cartoon Chaos | Wobbly, bubbly synthesized toots |
| Heavy Duty | Lower-pitched, longer rumbles |
| Musical Farts | A short sequence of musical pitches |

Built-in sounds are generated locally with Web Audio. Enabled custom files override the selected theme.

| Frequency | Approximate start-to-start interval |
| --- | --- |
| Gentle | 9 seconds |
| Standard | 4 seconds |
| Extreme | 1.2 seconds |

Timing varies slightly at random. Longer sounds finish before the next idle sound starts, with a short gap. Volume changes apply to the next sound. Zero volume silences playback without pausing monitoring.

## Development commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci` | Install locked dependencies |
| `npm run dev` | Run Vite and Electron together |
| `npm run build` | Build the production renderer into `dist/` |
| `npm start` | Open the desktop app using the production build |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the built UI in a browser |
| `npm test` | Run Electron end-to-end tests |
| `npm run package` | Build a portable Windows app |

**Browser limitation:** browser preview monitors activity inside its page only. Use Electron for inactivity detection across your computer.

## Build a Windows desktop app

```powershell
npm run package
```

Open `release/Fart Alert/Fart Alert.exe`. Keep the entire generated folder together: the executable needs its accompanying runtime files. This is a portable folder build, not an installer.

Generated dependencies, runtimes, caches, and build output are excluded from Git. This repository contains source code; build the executable locally unless a separate release is published. The packaging script currently targets Windows. macOS and Linux packages have not been configured or verified.

## Architecture and privacy

1. Electron's main process reads operating-system idle duration with `powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime()`.
2. An isolated preload bridge exposes that reading to the renderer through IPC.
3. The renderer checks the duration approximately every 250 ms against the configured timeout.
4. While idle and activated, it selects an enabled custom sound or synthesizes the chosen theme.
5. Framer Motion particles and the mascot respond to playback; further sounds follow the frequency setting.
6. Returning activity cancels pending playback and stops the current sound.

The app reads elapsed inactivity. It does not record typed keys, inspect other applications, capture screenshots, or save mouse trails. Node integration is disabled in the renderer and context isolation is enabled. There is no application backend, analytics service, or API key configuration.

```text
electron/
  main.cjs             Desktop window and system idle API
  preload.cjs          Isolated IPC bridge
src/
  main.jsx             Monitoring, settings, uploads, UI, particles
  audio.js             Web Audio synthesis and custom playback
  storage.js           IndexedDB sound persistence
  style.css            Base layout and mascot
  studio.css           Midnight palette, interface states and responsive refinements
scripts/package.mjs    Portable Windows packaging
tests/desktop.mjs      Electron end-to-end checks
tests/live-demo.mjs    Production browser and native idle demo
docs/images/           Project screenshots
vite.config.js         Renderer development and build settings
```

## Verification

The production desktop regression suite checks the native desktop idle API, upload auto-enabling, repeated custom playback and stopping with controlled idle readings, persistence after reload, theme fallback, preview, invalid files, deletion, and renderer errors.

The live demo uses elapsed inactivity without replacing the idle source. It checks three built-in themes, custom uploads and toggles, audio signal in the Web Audio graph, and persistence. In browser mode it also checks pointer return and narrow layout. The audio check measures the app signal, not physical speaker output.

After packaging, run:

```powershell
node tests/desktop.mjs --packaged
node tests/live-demo.mjs
node tests/live-demo.mjs --browser --url=https://fartalert.vercel.app
```

For the native demo, leave Windows idle until the test prints `SEND_REAL_INPUT_NOW`, then press a key in another app.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| No sound | Try **Test sound**, increase app and system volume, and check the audio output device. |
| No idle playback | Activate monitoring, then wait without using the computer. Use the desktop edition. |
| Theme is ignored | Disable all custom sounds; enabled uploads take priority. |
| File is rejected | Choose a decodable WAV or MP3 of 15 MB or less. |
| App will not start after cloning | Run `npm ci`, `npm run build`, then `npm start`. |
| Portable executable fails | Keep its accompanying runtime files in the generated folder. |
| Electron download runs out of space | Free disk space or put temporary files and the Electron download cache on a drive with space. |

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Include reproduction steps, operating system, selected theme and frequency, and whether custom sounds are enabled. Run the production build and relevant desktop tests before submitting playback changes.

## License

[ISC](LICENSE). Third-party packages retain their respective licenses.

---

*Stay curious. Stay hydrated. Stay upwind.*
