projects.readme:
# FitBox (DL & Computer Vision Fitness App)

**Your space. Your pace. Your fitness, one rep at a time.**

FitBox is an Android and web wellness app with on-device MediaPipe pose tracking, a local virtual coach, concealed daily tasks, Sweat/Goal Points, levels, goals, a 3D check-up reference, private video review, authenticated Neon sync and real Stripe sandbox billing.

**Project classification:** Deep learning / computer vision / fitness application. A pretrained neural pose model runs locally. Exercise phase rules and coaching are deterministic. This repository does not train a model and does not use a cloud LLM or Generative AI service at runtime. Pixel illustrations are generated development assets; animation sheets run locally.

| Try it | Link |
| --- | --- |
| Android test APK | [Download FitBox v0.5.2](https://github.com/vams2krish/fitbox-fitness-iot/releases/download/v0.5.2/FitBox-debug.apk) |
| Web app | [FitBox on Vercel](https://fitbox-fitness-iot.vercel.app) |
| Public source | [GitHub repository](https://github.com/vams2krish/fitbox-fitness-iot) |
| First design reference | [Original Figma, starting at 364:3661](https://www.figma.com/proto/7vS0ax0bayEIE4QrXlBjsQ/FitBox-App?node-id=364-3661&starting-point-node-id=364%3A3661) |

## Product showcase — Figma flow, refined

White, electric blue and violet with original pixel characters, animated workout/store sprites, an interactive digital athlete and streamlined camera HUD. Screens below are real app captures with fictional profiles. [Implementation and verification](docs/UI-REFINEMENT-v0.5.md).

| FitBox | Pixel coaches | Task Center |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![FitBox](docs/screenshots/70-fitbox-brand.png) | ![Coaches](docs/screenshots/71-pixel-trainers.png) | ![Home](docs/screenshots/84-interactive-athlete-hint.png) |
| Camera HUD | Goals | Store |
| ![Camera](docs/screenshots/76-camera-hud.png) | ![Goals](docs/screenshots/77-goal-journey.png) | ![Store](docs/screenshots/80-pixel-store.png) |
| Movement notes | Digital athlete | Private media |
| ![Instructions](docs/screenshots/78-movement-notes.png) | ![Athlete](docs/screenshots/85-athlete-shrink-control.png) | ![Local library](docs/screenshots/82-local-media-thumbnails.png) |

The five tabs retain their identity across screens. Goal Center and Store have dedicated Home entries; Reports lives beside Insights. Workout controls use progressive disclosure. A single canonical FitBox+ route handles all three Stripe sandbox plans. Completed tasks stay hidden until the eye toggle is selected.

Exercise instruction dialogs show one centered looping character, with no coach portrait or duplicate still image.

### Looping pixel artwork

32 individual sprite sheets cover two coaches, all 24 exercises and six store goodies. [Browse PNG strips and GIF exports](web/assets/design/sprites). Six illustrated poses per loop are packed into twelve runtime frames; off-screen animation pauses and reduced-motion displays a still.

| Pushups | Squats | Studio cap | Shaker |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ![Pushups](web/assets/design/sprites/pushups.gif) | ![Squats](web/assets/design/sprites/squats.gif) | ![Cap](web/assets/design/sprites/store-studio-cap.gif) | ![Shaker](web/assets/design/sprites/store-shaker.gif) |

Source atlases and exact prompts are in [the art manifest](docs/source-atlases/manifest.json); `python tools/pack-sprite-atlases.py` recreates the runtime sheets. These illustrations demonstrate movement rather than assessing the camera user's form.

## Connected product journey

| Area | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| First-time experience | Choose John/Tina, select multiple categories from Muscle Exercise / Physical Training / Yoga / Meditation / Aerobics / Zumba, provide name/report email, answer guided preferences, and complete a replayable four-step tutorial |
| Task Center | All unfinished tasks start concealed. Reveal only the current eligible task. Complete and claim it to unlock the next mystery; later exercise identities stay hidden |
| Congratulations | Actual saved reps, active time, SP earned, total GP, level and tasks done. Partial sessions still accumulate; incomplete goals cannot be claimed |
| Task done | A claimed task shows a persistent Task done label and its 25 GP award |
| Sweat Points | One SP per saved rep plus one SP per five tracked hold seconds. Manual timed practice uses active seconds. Counts are derived from history, not a mutable currency balance |
| Goal Points and levels | One claim per task/day awards 25 GP. Every 100 GP advances a level and opens an earned Level up screen with upcoming milestones |
| Goal Center | Daily totals, point rules, level progress and up to eight personal daily targets for reps, minutes or claimed tasks. Custom targets do not manufacture GP |
| Virtual coach | New John/Tina coach symbols, a draggable in-app avatar bubble, unread local notifications, daily check-ins and day-end report prompts |
| Doubt Center | Local answers from exercise instructions and FAQ for tracking, points, mystery tasks, membership and reports; linked Message Center |
| Learning Center | Exercise search across names, descriptions and instructions; categories, favorites, practiced labels, guides and camera setup |
| Checkup Center | Blender-adapted detailed digital athlete with drag/keyboard rotation, front/back controls and wheel/pinch zoom; real saved activity statistics; 2D fallback on unsupported devices |
| Go premium | Subscribe me pricing popup and three real sandbox memberships; checkout, authoritative status and customer billing/cancellation management |
| Premium appearance | Crown and gold coach-avatar rim appear only after server-confirmed sandbox entitlement. A redirect query cannot activate membership |
| End of day | Finish-day confirmation, daily analysis and a 1–5 experience popup labelled Poor / Fair / Okay / Good / Excellent. Reviews persist by day |
| Daily report email | Account setup requires a report email, editable in Account details. Daily analysis previews use that address. Delivery remains demo-only by request: nothing is sent |
| Local review | Video import, playback, favorites and confirmed deletion; optional silent one-minute / 50 MB practice recordings remain on the device |
| Accounts and sync | Better Auth email/password accounts, HttpOnly sessions, consent-gated scalar workout sync and selected profile preferences on Neon Postgres |

Revealing a task never costs points or money. There are no paid random rewards. SP/GP are app progress points, not measurements of sweat, body composition or health. Manual records remain user-controlled practice data.

## Three sandbox membership plans

| Plan | Recurring period | USD total per period |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starter | 3 months | $20.99 |
| Plus | 6 months | $36.99 |
| Pro | 12 months | $60.99 |

The totals follow the source plan amounts. Plans renew each selected period until canceled. Live Stripe keys/events are refused. Checkout accepts only a server-whitelisted plan ID; clients cannot choose amounts. Signed webhooks are processed idempotently, and fresh provider state handles activation, cancellation and expiry. Pending checkouts are reused and existing subscriptions prevent duplicate purchases. All training features remain free during this beta; subscriptions test billing and premium appearance without charging real money.

## Camera task matrix

There are **24 tasks: 15 pose tasks (9 rep tasks and 6 holds), plus 9 explicitly manual activities**. All automatic tasks use an ordinary RGB camera; no depth sensor is required. Front/Side describe body orientation relative to the lens, independent of which phone lens is selected. External cameras work only when the browser/WebView exposes them.

| Exercise | Task | View | Setup / limitation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pushups | Pose reps | Side | Place the camera low, side-on. Keep your shoulders, hips and ankles in frame. |
| Squats | Pose reps | Side | Place the camera around hip height, side-on, with your whole body visible. |
| Stationary lunges | Pose reps | Side | Stand side-on. Keep both feet and your full body visible. Track one set on each side. |
| Plank | Pose hold | Side | Place the camera low, side-on. Your shoulder, hip, knee and ankle must be visible. |
| Situps | Pose reps | Side | Place the camera low, side-on. Keep your shoulders, hips, knees and feet in frame. |
| Crunches | Pose reps | Side | Use a low side view. Keep the camera fixed and shoulders, hips and knees visible. |
| Pullups | Pose reps | Front | Face the camera. Include the bar, both hands, elbows, shoulders and hips. |
| Biceps curls | Pose reps | Side | Stand side-on, camera near chest height, with the working arm fully visible. |
| Glute bridges | Pose reps | Side | Use a low side view that includes shoulders, hips, knees and feet. |
| Jumping jacks | Pose reps | Front | Face the camera. Allow room above your hands and to both sides of your feet. |
| Chair pose | Pose hold | Side | Use a full-body side view with feet visible. |
| Mountain pose | Pose hold | Front | Face the camera, keeping your whole body and feet visible. |
| Warrior II | Pose hold | Front | Face the camera with both arms and feet visible. Leave room to either side. |
| Tree pose | Pose hold | Front | Face the camera. Stand near a stable support if you need one. |
| Downward-facing dog | Pose hold | Side | Place the camera low and side-on, with hands and feet visible. |
| Burpees | Manual practice | Not required | Use the manual timer or repetition counter. Automatic counting has not been validated for this activity. |
| Walking / treadmill | Manual practice | Not required | Use the manual timer or repetition counter. Automatic counting has not been validated for this activity. |
| Stationary cycling | Manual practice | Not required | Use the manual timer or repetition counter. Automatic counting has not been validated for this activity. |
| Shadow boxing | Manual practice | Not required | Use the manual timer or repetition counter. Automatic counting has not been validated for this activity. |
| Handstand | Manual practice | Not required | Use the manual timer or repetition counter. Automatic counting has not been validated for this activity. |
| Bench press | Manual practice | Not required | Use the manual timer or repetition counter. Automatic counting has not been validated for this activity. |
| Mindful breathing | Manual practice | Not required | Use the manual timer or repetition counter. Automatic counting has not been validated for this activity. |
| Aerobics practice | Manual practice | Not required | Use the manual timer or repetition counter. Automatic counting has not been validated for this activity. |
| Zumba practice | Manual practice | Not required | Use the manual timer or repetition counter. Automatic counting has not been validated for this activity. |

## On-device AI and 3D

The APK bundles MediaPipe Pose Landmarker Lite float16 version 1 and @mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.2.3 with its WASM runtime. Android uses CPU WASM to avoid WebView GPU-driver variability; other browsers try GPU with CPU fallback. The model produces 33 landmarks in memory. Visibility thresholds, neutral calibration, stable phase transitions, aspect-corrected joint angles, cooldowns and timestamp-gap resets feed repetition/hold rules. Tracking pauses when the required joints or a single person are not visible.

Model SHA-256: 59929e1d1ee95287735ddd833b19cf4ac46d29bc7afddbbf6753c459690d574a. See [model provenance](web/models/manifest.json), [MediaPipe runtime license](web/vendor/mediapipe/LICENSE) and [official pose documentation](https://ai.google.dev/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/pose_landmarker).

Checkup uses bundled Three.js 0.187.0 with its [MIT license](web/vendor/three/LICENSE). The detailed male and illustrative female digital athletes are Blender adaptations of an openly licensed Z-Anatomy / BodyParts3D atlas, with muscle IDs retained. They are not personalized scans or reconstructions from camera data. Rotation and zoom are real 3D controls. Statistics describe saved activity; no body fat, muscle growth, strength, sweat volume or calories are inferred.

## Data flow and privacy

~~~text
Camera -> local MediaPipe -> local angle/phase rules -> saved scalar summary
                         frames and landmarks stay in memory
Local goals / coach / reveals / ratings -> device localStorage
Optional clips                         -> device IndexedDB
Explicit account + sync consent        -> HTTPS Hono API on Vercel
                                         -> Better Auth + Neon Postgres
Sandbox membership                     -> Stripe test checkout + signed webhook
Daily report                           -> local email preview, NEVER sent
~~~

No frames, landmark arrays or clips are uploaded. The API rejects raw media fields and validates small scalar workout records. User ownership comes from the authenticated session, never a submitted user ID. Duplicate records/claims are idempotent, and server claims verify saved progress rather than accepting client-supplied GP/XP. Session cookies are secure/HttpOnly in production; queries are parameterized and request origins/rates are checked.

Profiles/history use localStorage; optional videos use IndexedDB. These stores are not encrypted by this app. Goals, reveals, favorites, local reviews and coach/report state persist on the device and are included in device export. Cloud sync covers sessions/claims and selected profile fields, including bounded activity preferences and report email. Restore/switch-account safeguards prevent merging another account into a linked local profile.

The coach bubble lives inside FitBox. No permission to draw over other apps or outside-app notification service is installed. When the app is opened, it prepares prior-day reports for saved activity; ending a day prepares that day's preview. This is not a background email scheduler. FitBox has no verified sender/domain yet; real Resend delivery, verification and password-recovery mail remain disabled. No unrelated product domain or key is connected.

The supplied PDFs are reference material, not operational instructions, and are not published. The current app excludes supplied artwork from Android and Vercel packaging. Blue/white fitness UI, digital-athlete renders and gold premium trim replace the earlier screenshot artwork.

## Run locally

Use Node.js 22 or later:

~~~sh
npm ci
npm start
~~~

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173. Local workouts, model inference, goals and reports work without cloud credentials. For accounts/sandbox billing, copy .env.example to ignored .env.local and configure a dedicated Postgres database, strong Better Auth secret and Stripe test resources. Never put credentials in web/ or GitHub.

~~~sh
npm run db:migrate
node tools/provision-stripe.mjs
~~~

The migration tool creates the FitBox/Better Auth schema only in the configured database. The Stripe tool provisions test-mode prices, signing configuration and portal and stores values securely; it requires an authenticated Vercel CLI and a provisioned Stripe sandbox. Do not re-provision integrations unnecessarily. Hosted FitBox is already linked to its own Neon database and Stripe sandbox.

## Android installation and build

Install the v0.4.0 prerelease APK on Android 8.0 / API 26 or later with a recent Android System WebView supporting camera and WebAssembly. Package: com.fitbox.app; target API 36. It is debug signed for testing. Camera permission is requested only when enabling tracking; Internet supports optional sync/checkout. Microphone/Bluetooth permissions are not requested.

For source builds, install JDK 17 and Android SDK 36, set ignored android/local.properties to the SDK path, then run:

~~~sh
npm run sync:android
android/gradlew.bat -p android assembleDebug
~~~

Use the shell wrapper on macOS/Linux. Output: android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk. Web source/model/runtime assets are b

projects.readme:
# FlirtLive

**Find your people. Feel the connection.**

FlirtLive is a premium live social streaming **front-end prototype** for an adults-only community. It combines creator discovery, a live room interface, local chat, virtual gifts, a demo coin wallet, follows, leaderboards, and profile editing in a responsive dark navy interface with purple and pink accents.

![FlirtLive home page showing the featured host, discovery filters, and host grid](flirtlive-home.png)

## Project showcase

The home screenshot above is an actual capture from the initial demo build. Additional live-room, discovery, leaderboard, wallet, profile, and mobile captures are pending browser access; no generated mockups are presented as tested application screenshots.

## Project status

This is an interactive browser demo, not an operational webcam service. Host identities, viewer counts, rankings, messages, and stream status are sample data. Room backgrounds are still portraits, not live video. The pictured models are stock-photo subjects and are not represented as actual platform hosts. No explicit content is included.

The private hosted preview is available to its owner at [FlirtLive preview](https://flirtlive-social-lounge.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site). Public repository access does not grant access to that private preview.

## Features

| Area | Current experience |
| --- | --- |
| Home | Featured hero, host cards, live badges, country labels, categories, and sample viewer counts |
| Discover | Search hosts by name, country, and interests; category and country filtering |
| Live room | Portrait stage, host information, follow action, share action, and local chat composition |
| Virtual gifts | Rose, Love, Diamond, Teddy Bear, Crown, and Rocket; sending deducts demo coins |
| Coin wallet | Starting balance of 1,250 test coins; simulated package top-ups without payment |
| Following | Follow/unfollow hosts and browse saved favorites |
| Top Live | Sample weekly rankings and a top-three podium |
| Messages | Sample creator invitations linking to their rooms; not private messaging |
| Profile | Editable display name and bio, local profile-photo upload, following and gifting stats |
| Host onboarding | Interest dialog saved on the current device; no camera capture or broadcast |
| Responsive UI | Sidebar navigation, mobile layouts, gradients, translucent panels, and hover transitions |

## Run locally

No package installation, API key, or build step is required. Install Python 3 and serve the static files:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/FlirtLive.git
cd FlirtLive
python -m http.server 4173 --directory dist
```

Open [http://localhost:4173](http://localhost:4173). Stop the server with `Ctrl+C`.

Alternatively, use any static HTTP server with `dist/` as the document root. Deploy that same directory to a static hosting provider.

## Pages and routes

| Route | Page |
| --- | --- |
| `#home` | Featured content and live host grid |
| `#discover` | Host browser |
| `#room/1` | Example host room; IDs 1–8 are available |
| `#following` | Saved follows |
| `#top` | Leaderboard |
| `#coins` | Demo wallet and gift catalog |
| `#messages` | Sample invitations |
| `#profile` | Profile editor |

Navigation uses URL hashes, so a static server needs no route rewrites. Press `Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K` to focus search.

## Technology and structure

- Semantic HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript; no application framework or build dependencies.
- CSS Grid/Flexbox, responsive media queries, and Google Fonts (DM Sans and Manrope).
- Sample portraits loaded from Unsplash image URLs.
- Browser `localStorage` for demo preferences and wallet/profile state.

```text
FlirtLive/
├── dist/
│   ├── index.html          # Application shell and navigation
│   ├── style.css           # Theme, components, and responsive styles
│   └── app.js              # Demo data, routing, rendering, and interactions
├── flirtlive-home.png       # Project screenshot


├── .gitignore
└── README.md
```

## Data behavior and limitations

The `flirtlive` localStorage entry stores the coin balance, following list, profile name/bio/avatar, and coins gifted. The separate `hostInterest` entry stores hosting interest. These values belong to one browser on one device; they are not synchronized, authenticated, or tamper-resistant. Clear those entries to reset the demo. Room chat messages and gift notifications persist locally, with up to 100 entries per room. They are not shared with other users. Do not use the demo for sensitive information or real monetary balances.

Photo uploads accept image files up to 2 MB and store them locally. Large images can exceed browser storage quotas. External images and fonts require an internet connection. Profile XP and level indicators are illustrative, not a progression engine.

## Production roadmap

To turn this interface into an operational platform, the remaining work includes:

1. Authentication, account recovery, persistent user profiles, and authorization.
2. A real streaming provider/WebRTC implementation, host publishing, viewer playback, and presence.
3. Shared room chat and private messaging with server persistence and abuse controls.
4. Server-authoritative wallet accounting, payment processing, gift transactions, refunds, and creator payouts.
5. Age and creator identity verification, consent workflows, moderation, reporting/blocking, and operational policies appropriate to the intended service.
6. Real discovery, rankings, follow counts, media storage, analytics, and administration.
7. Automated tests, accessibility review, performance work, deployment configuration, monitoring, and security review.

The current browser demo has no backend, database, payment integration, streaming service, or real age-verification mechanism. An “18+” label is not verification.

## Validation

Run `node --check dist/app.js` and `node --test tests/demo.test.cjs`. Five regression tests cover routes/discovery, wallet/gifts, chat/follow persistence, profile saving, and storage recovery using a simulated DOM. See [the verification report](docs/VERIFICATION.md) for evidence and limits. Fresh live browser verification and additional page screenshots are pending because browser use is disabled in Work settings.

## Images and licensing

The screenshot documents this project's interface. Portrait imagery is loaded from Unsplash; the source image identifiers are listed in `dist/app.js`. Review the applicable image terms and replace placeholder assets before production use. Third-party imagery and fonts retain their respective rights. No open-source software license has been selected for this repository.

projects.readme:
# PDRides — Full-Stack Ride-Sharing Application

**Public-Demand Ride-share Made Easy**

PDRides is a community ride-sharing web application that connects passengers and drivers through a browser interface and messaging integrations. The project brings together ride discovery, driver ride offers, seat booking, route planning, estimated fares, account settings, and advertising configuration. Its product goal is a platform with no platform fees for passengers or drivers.

![PDRides project screenshot showing the home page and messaging entry points](docs/images/pdrides-home.png)

*Actual project home page captured locally. Marketing statements displayed in the interface are product copy, not independently verified usage or service guarantees.*

[Source code](https://github.com/vams2krish/FullStack-PDRides) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/vams2krish/FullStack-PDRides/issues)

[Open the live Vercel UI showcase](https://pdrides-showcase.vercel.app) · Browse the redesigned screens. Live accounts, bookings, and messaging are disabled in the showcase.

## Product showcase

Actual locally rendered project screens. These show the interface; successful production authentication and bookings have not been verified.

### Passenger and driver login

![Passenger and driver role selection](docs/images/pdrides-login.png)

Role selection before phone verification.

### Registration

![Multi-step passenger and driver registration](docs/images/pdrides-register.png)

Personal information, contact details, and preferences. OTP delivery and persisted registration require a working database.

### Map and trip planning

![OpenStreetMap tiles, pickup and destination, and fare controls](docs/images/pdrides-map.png)

Map tiles render successfully. Location access was unavailable, as shown in the screenshot. Fare calculation and bookings were not verified.

### Help center

![Help center topics and frequently asked questions](docs/images/pdrides-help.png)

Support topics for accounts, rides, payments, safety, and technical questions.

## Live verification status

**Production end-to-end verification is still pending.** Local checks exercise the actual Express routes, screen rendering, authorization gates, and booking validation. A reachable test MongoDB and messaging sandbox are required to verify persisted bookings and OTP delivery.

Read the [verification report](docs/verification-2026-10-29.md) for evidence, production blockers, and remaining acceptance steps. No real messages, production bookings, or account changes were performed.

### Browse rides

![Ride discovery filters and empty state](docs/images/pdrides-browse.png)

### Contact and support

![PDRides contact and support page](docs/images/pdrides-contact.png)

## Project overview

Drivers can publish trips with pickup and destination details, timing, available seats, and a contribution amount. Passengers can discover rides and use booking flows. Map services supply location search, routing, distance, and fare estimates. WhatsApp supports messaging and phone verification; Telegram webhook and bot service modules are also included. MongoDB stores users, rides, conversations, and advertisements.

This repository is an application prototype with implemented backend routes and frontend screens. Messaging requires configured provider accounts. Seat bookings use published rides; simulated driver assignment has been retired. A screenshot or a successful server start does not establish that all integrations are working in production.

## Features and implementation

| Area | Included in the codebase |
| --- | --- |
| Ride discovery | Browse rides, filter by trip details, view shared ride pages, and see seat availability |
| Driver tools | Publish and manage ride offers with vehicle/profile information |
| Passenger tools | Book seats, cancel bookings, and review ride history |
| Maps | Leaflet interface, OpenStreetMap tiles, Nominatim location lookup, and OSRM routing |
| Fare estimates | Distance/time calculations, ride-type pricing, and detailed fare breakdowns |
| Accounts | WhatsApp OTP flows, registration, sessions, profile and driver settings |
| Preferences | Favorite routes, recent searches, privacy and notification settings |
| Messaging | WhatsApp Cloud API service/webhook and Telegram bot service/webhook |
| Advertising | Ad models, API routes, placement configuration, geographic targeting, and fallback content |
| Maintenance | Scheduled ride expiration and completion tasks; application/database health routes |

## Design system

The shared stylesheet uses deep pine for navigation, teal for actions, mint for highlights, and a light neutral canvas. Amber marks keyboard focus. The theme is shared across the landing, account, trip, and support screens.

## Technology

- **Frontend:** HTML, CSS, browser JavaScript, and Leaflet.
- **Backend:** Node.js with ECMAScript modules and Express 4.
- **Persistence:** MongoDB, Mongoose 8, and the MongoDB Node.js driver 7.
- **Integrations:** WhatsApp Cloud API, Telegram Bot API, Nominatim, and OSRM.
- **Utilities:** Axios, dotenv, node-cron, and nodemon for development.

## Vercel showcase

The public showcase is a static build of the application screens. Run `node scripts/build-showcase.mjs` to generate `showcase-dist/`; the Vercel configuration publishes only that directory. Use the Express application below for MongoDB-backed flows.

## Local setup

### Prerequisites

- Node.js **20.19 or newer**, matching the minimum required by the declared MongoDB 7 driver dependency.
- npm and a reachable MongoDB instance, locally or hosted.
- A Meta WhatsApp Cloud API application for WhatsApp delivery and OTP testing.
- A Telegram bot token if testing Telegram integration.

### Install and configure

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/FullStack-PDRides.git
cd FullStack-PDRides
npm install
```

Copy the environment template:

```powershell
# PowerShell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

```bash
# macOS / Linux
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env` with your own configuration. Use the same port in `PORT` and `WEB_APP_URL`; the template currently has different values. A consistent local example is:

```dotenv
PORT=3000
NODE_ENV=development
APP_NAME=PDRides
MONGODB_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017/pdrides
WEB_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID=your_phone_number_id
WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN=your_access_token
WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN=your_verification_token
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=your_bot_token
TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=your_webhook_secret
MAX_RIDE_RESULTS=5
```

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `PORT` | HTTP port; the server falls back to `3002` when unset |
| `MONGODB_URI` | Database connection; `MONGO_URI` and `MONGODB_URL` are fallback aliases |
| `MONGODB_DATABASE` | Optional database name; defaults to `pdrides` |
| `WEB_APP_URL` | Base URL used for links sent in messages |
| `APP_NAME` | Optional display name in server/health output |
| `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID` | Your Meta WhatsApp phone-number resource ID |
| `WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Credential for WhatsApp message delivery |
| `WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN` | Value used during webhook verification |
| `WHATSAPP_API_VERSION` | Optional Graph API version override used by the WhatsApp service |
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | Telegram bot credential |
| `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Telegram webhook configuration secret |
| `MAX_RIDE_RESULTS` | Ride-result configuration from the environment template |

The template also contains `MAPBOX_TOKEN` and `OPENROUTESERVICE_KEY`; the current map service uses Nominatim and OSRM directly. Keep `.env` private and replace the example phone-number ID with your own.

Some integration modules read environment variables during module initialization. If credentials from `.env` are not picked up with `npm start`, preload the file before importing the app:

```bash
node --env-file=.env src/index.js
```

### Run

```bash
npm run dev
# or
npm start
```

The backend connects to MongoDB before opening its HTTP listener. With the configuration above, visit `http://localhost:3000/`.

## Screens and routes

| URL | Screen |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Home page |
| `/map` | Interactive map and trip planning |
| `/register` | Registration |
| `/login` | Login |
| `/browse-all-rides` | Ride discovery |
| `/my-rides` | Personal rides |
| `/ride/:id` | Shareable ride details |
| `/settings` | Account and preferences |
| `/ads-config` | Advertising configuration interface |
| `/help-center` | Help content |
| `/contact-us` | Contact page |
| `/privacy-policy` | Privacy policy |
| `/terms-of-service` | Terms of service |

The static HTML files are also present at the repository root. Opening only those files does not supply the API or database functionality.

## API overview

| Endpoint or group | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | Application liveness |
| `GET /api/health`, `GET /api/ping` | Database-aware health and connectivity |
| `/api/auth/*` | OTP requests, verification, registration, and session operations |
| `/api/user/*` | Profile, vehicle details, preferences, and history |
| `/api/users/me/*` | Unified current-user profile and preferences routes |
| `GET /api/rides`, `POST /api/rides` | Search and create ride offers |
| `/api/rides/:id/*` | Ride booking, cancellation, completion, and status operations |
| `GET /api/fare` | Fare estimates for pickup/destination locations |
| `POST /api/ride/book` | Retired prototype endpoint; returns HTTP 410 |
| `GET /api/route` | Route details |
| `GET /api/autocomplete`, `GET /api/reverse-geocode` | Location lookup |
| `/api/ads*` | Advertisement management and delivery routes |
| `/webhook` | WhatsApp verification and incoming events |
| `/telegram-webhook` | Telegram incoming events |

Consult [the app entry point](src/index.js) and [route modules](src/routes) for request fields and authorization behavior. Some ride and location routes are defined in the entry point before the unified API router; Express handles the first matching route, so overlapping handlers need to be considered when extending the API.

## Messaging setup

**WhatsApp:** Configure your own Meta credentials and verification token, expose the app through an HTTPS URL, and configure the callback at `/webhook`. Subscribe the provider application to the events needed by the webhook handlers. OTP and outgoing-message flows require working provider credentials.

**Telegram:** Configure your own bot token and webhook settings. [set-telegram-webhook.js](set-telegram-webhook.js) is the repository's setup helper; inspect its configuration before running it against a bot. The source includes both Telegram and WhatsApp integrations, but their presence does not confirm a deployed bot is online.

## Repository layout

```text
FullStack-PDRides/
├── index.html                 # Landing page
├── map-view.html              # Map and trip planning UI
├── browse-rides.html           # Ride discovery UI
├── my-rides.html               # Personal ride UI
├── ride-details.html           # Shared ride UI
├── login.html / register.html  # Account entry screens
├── settings.html               # User preferences
├── ads-config.html             # Advertising UI
├── css/                        # Screen styles
├── src/
│   ├── index.js                # Express app, routes, startup
│   ├── middleware/             # Authentication helpers
│   ├── models/                 # User, Ride, Conversation, Ad
│   ├── routes/                 # Auth, user, API, messaging, ads
│   └── services/               # Database, rides, maps, messaging, scheduling
├── ads-config/                 # Placement, targeting, unit and fallback JSON
├── ads-system/                 # Ad loader and developer configuration
├── docs/images/                # README project screenshot
├── test-*.js / test-*.json      # Manual integration scripts and sample payloads
├── .env.example                # Environment template
└── package.json                # Dependencies and commands
```

## Verification and current limitations

Run `npm test` for the HTTP integration and booking validation checks. Live database and messaging acceptance still requires a configured test environment.

For a configured local instance:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/health
curl http://localhost:3000/api/health
```

Then exercise registration, an offered ride, ride discovery, booking/cancellation, and the messaging callbacks with test accounts.

Before production use, verify the deployed database, provider callbacks, authorization, and full driver-to-passenger booking and cancellation flow.

## Contributing

Open an issue with reproduction steps or a proposed improvement. For code changes, describe the affected flow, configuration needs, and how it was verified. Do not include credentials, personal ride data, or production message payloads.

## License

`package.json` declares MIT, but this repository currently has no standalone `LICENSE` file. Confirm the intended license terms with the repository owner before relying on a license grant.

projects.name: GenAI-Game-Industry-Research-Agents
projects.description: CrewAI multi-agent Python prototype: a Senior Researcher and Writer use Serper web search, sequential tasks, memory, and caching to produce games-industry articles. Includes setup instructions and a project architecture image.
projects.readme:
# GenAI Game Industry Research Agents

![CrewAI project overview: researcher, writer, and Markdown article](docs/project-overview.svg)

A Python experiment that coordinates a **Senior Researcher** and a **Writer** with CrewAI. The crew searches the web through Serper, investigates technology trends in the games industry, and turns its findings into a Markdown article.

## Project summary

This repository demonstrates role-based agents, tool use, sequential tasks, memory, and caching in one readable script. It is a learning prototype rather than a deployed application. The project image above is an architecture illustration, not a screenshot of a user interface.

## How the workflow works

1. The researcher searches for games-industry trends and evaluates benefits, market opportunities, and risks.
2. The research task requests a three-paragraph report.
3. The writer runs after the researcher in a sequential crew and writes an accessible four-paragraph article.
4. CrewAI saves the article to `new-blog-post2.md`, and the script prints the final result.

| Component | Configuration in the script |
| --- | --- |
| Senior Researcher | Web search, verbose logging, memory, delegation enabled |
| Writer | Web search, verbose logging, memory, delegation disabled |
| Search tool | `SerperDevTool` |
| Execution | `Process.sequential` |
| Crew settings | Memory and caching enabled; `max_rpm=100` |
| Output | Markdown file plus terminal output |

## Repository contents

```text
app.py                       Agent definitions, tasks, crew, and execution
requirements.txt             Python dependencies (unpinned)
.env.example                 Placeholder environment variable names
.gitignore                   Excludes secrets, caches, and generated output
new-blog-post.md              Historical sample output from a different topic
README.md                    Project documentation
docs/project-overview.svg    Project architecture image
```

The historical `new-blog-post.md` discusses a different industry and contains unverified claims. It is retained as an existing artifact and is not representative of the current games-industry prompts or a validated research result.

## Setup

Use a Python version supported by your installed CrewAI release. See the [official CrewAI installation guide](https://docs.crewai.com/en/installation) for current requirements.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/GenAI-Game-Industry-Research-Agents.git
cd GenAI-Game-Industry-Research-Agents
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

On macOS/Linux, activate the environment with `source .venv/bin/activate`.

### Credentials

The script reads two environment variables. Set them in the terminal where you run the project:

```powershell
$env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY"
$env:SERPER_API_KEY = "YOUR_SERPER_API_KEY"
python app.py
```

For macOS/Linux:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY"
export SERPER_API_KEY="YOUR_SERPER_API_KEY"
python app.py
```

`.env.example` is a reference only: the script does not automatically load `.env` files. Never put real credentials in source control. Missing credentials cause a clear error before the crew is constructed. Obtain credentials from [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/) and [Serper](https://serper.dev/). Running the crew makes external API calls and may incur charges.

## Customizing the crew

Edit the agent `role`, `goal`, and `backstory` fields to change responsibilities. Adjust each task's `description` and `expected_output` to control the research scope and article structure. Change `output_file` to choose a different destination.

The `topic` passed to `crew.kickoff()` is currently not referenced through a `{topic}` placeholder in the task descriptions. Changing that input alone will not retarget the hardcoded games-industry prompts; edit the prompts as well. The research task's expected output mentions AI trends, while its description covers games-industry trends more broadly.

## Limitations and validation

- This is an older CrewAI example. Dependencies are unpinned, and compatibility with current releases has not been established. Settings such as `share_crew=True` may require review against the installed version.
- No model is explicitly selected in the script; model behavior and access depend on CrewAI configuration and provider defaults.
- Memory may require additional provider configuration and local storage, depending on the installed release.
- Search results and generated claims need human verification. The script does not enforce citations or fact-check its output.
- Verbose logs can contain prompts, research, and generated text. Review the configured sharing and logging behavior before processing private information.
- Publication checks cover Python syntax, repository contents, and credential removal. A live paid API run has not been performed.

## Suggested next steps

Pin and test compatible dependency versions, parameterize the topic in all prompts, add explicit source citations, and make model selection configurable. A CLI and repeatable integration tests would make the prototype easier to maintain.

## References

- [CrewAI source and documentation](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI)
- [CrewAI installation](https://docs.crewai.com/en/installation)
- [Serper](https://serper.dev/)

## License

No license has been selected for this project. Add an appropriate license before granting reuse rights beyond those provided by GitHub's terms.

projects.readme:
# GenAI Job Apply Bot

**A Python job-search assistant that discovers roles, scores matches, prepares applications, and tracks outcomes—with optional generative AI cover letters and Telegram control.**

![Dashboard preview using sample data](docs/images/dashboard-preview.png)

*Illustrative dashboard preview with sample data. The figures are demonstration values, not measured performance claims; the current dashboard layout may differ slightly.*

## Project overview

Job Apply Bot brings job discovery, application preparation, and application tracking into one local workflow. It reads public company job boards, filters roles against an applicant's preferences, fills supported forms with Playwright, and records results in SQLite. A Streamlit dashboard makes application history searchable, while Telegram provides notifications and interactive controls.

**Project type: automation with optional GenAI integration.** Matching uses explicit rules and keyword scores, not a trained ML or deep-learning model. Generative AI is optional: Anthropic can draft cover letters from resume text, and OpenRouter can interpret Telegram requests. The core discovery and matching workflow does not require an AI API key.

This public edition contains source code, anonymous configuration examples, and a sample dashboard image. Personal resumes, application documents, credentials, screenshots, and live databases are excluded. It starts with automatic submission disabled.

## Features

- **Company job-board discovery:** Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby APIs, with discovery adapters for Workable and SmartRecruiters.
- **Explainable matching:** target titles, acceptable locations, excluded words, keyword scores, and optional sponsorship-related posting exclusions.
- **Browser form assistance:** Playwright form filling for Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby, including resume and cover-letter uploads.
- **Review handling:** unsupported required questions, CAPTCHA, and site blocks can stop automated progress and require manual review.
- **Cover letters:** an optional local Word document, an optional Anthropic-generated letter, or a basic template, exported to PDF.
- **Answer bank:** an optional Word table containing approved regex-to-answer mappings.
- **Application records:** SQLite job history, statuses, notes, durations, and screenshot references.
- **Dashboard:** date, status, company, platform, score, and text filters, plus outcome and activity charts.
- **Telegram:** application notifications, status menus, pause/resume controls, and optional natural-language command routing.
- **Email application path:** a separate Gmail SMTP command for eligible postings that explicitly request applications by email.
- **Execution options:** local CLI, manually scheduled runs, and a Docker image.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Company job boards] --> B[Discover roles]
    P[Applicant profile and settings] --> C[Rule-based matching]
    B --> D[(SQLite)]
    D --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E[Playwright application assistant]
    R[Local resume and optional answer bank] --> E
    R --> F[Cover-letter generation]
    F --> E
    E --> D
    D --> G[Streamlit dashboard]
    D --> H[Telegram summaries and control]
```

## Technology stack

| Area | Technology |
| --- | --- |
| Runtime | Python; Python 3.12 is a practical starting point |
| HTTP and discovery | HTTPX |
| Browser automation | Playwright / Chromium |
| Configuration | YAML / PyYAML |
| Persistence | SQLite |
| Dashboard | Streamlit, pandas, Altair |
| Document handling | pypdf, ReportLab, python-docx |
| Optional GenAI | Anthropic SDK; OpenRouter HTTP API |
| Notifications / email | Telegram Bot API; Gmail SMTP |
| Container | Playwright Python Docker image |

## Quick start (Windows PowerShell)

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/GenAI-Job-Apply-Bot.git
cd GenAI-Job-Apply-Bot
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m playwright install chromium
Copy-Item config/profile.example.yaml config/profile.yaml
Copy-Item .env.example .env
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force data/resume
```

1. Edit `config/profile.yaml` with your own contact details, target roles, locations, and truthful application answers. Replace every sample value before filling forms.
2. Save your PDF resume at `data/resume/base.pdf`, or change `resume_file` in `config/settings.yaml`.
3. Review the company slugs in `config/companies.yaml`; job boards and listings can change.
4. Keep `auto_submit: false` while checking form behavior. `JOBBOT_DRY_RUN=1` also forces dry-run mode.
5. Configure Telegram credentials in `.env` if you want notifications. Leave optional provider credentials empty unless you use those features.

```powershell
$env:JOBBOT_DRY_RUN = '1'
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m jobbot --help
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m jobbot verify
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m jobbot discover
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m jobbot match
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m jobbot stats
# Fills eligible forms without submitting; requires your local resume/profile.
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m jobbot apply --limit 1
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m streamlit run src/jobbot/dashboard.py
```

On macOS/Linux, create the environment with `python3 -m venv .venv`, use `.venv/bin/python`, copy examples with `cp`, and export environment variables with your shell. Linux may require `python -m playwright install --with-deps chromium`.

## Configuration

| File / variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `config/profile.example.yaml` | Anonymous starting profile; copy to the ignored `config/profile.yaml` |
| `config/settings.yaml` | Score threshold, daily cap, delays, browser mode, resume path, and submission mode |
| `config/companies.yaml` | Company names, ATS types, and board identifiers |
| `config/Cover_Letter.docx` | Optional personal letter; supports `{company}` and `{title}` placeholders |
| `config/Application_Answer_Bank.docx` | Optional Word table: `Use?`, regex, answer, source; enabled rows begin with `Y` |
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` | Telegram notifications and chat control |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Optional AI cover-letter generation |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_MODEL` | Optional natural-language Telegram routing; set a valid model identifier |
| `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` | Optional Gmail SMTP credentials; sender uses the profile email |
| `JOBBOT_DB` | Override the default `data/jobbot.sqlite` path |
| `JOBBOT_DRY_RUN` | Any nonempty value forces `auto_submit` off; unset it to stop overriding settings |

For AI cover letters, set `use_ai_cover_letter: true` and `cover_letter_mode: ai`. Review `MODEL` in `src/jobbot/tailor.py` and choose a model available to your Anthropic account; the bundled identifier is not verified. API failures fall back to the basic template. Generated content should be reviewed for accuracy. Resume text and job descriptions are sent to the configured provider when this feature is enabled. Natural-language Telegram routing sends chat text to OpenRouter when configured.

## CLI reference

Run commands as `python -m jobbot COMMAND [--limit N]` from the project root using your virtual environment.

| Command | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `verify` | Check configured company job boards |
| `discover` | Fetch jobs into the local database |
| `match` | Score new jobs and update matching/skipped states |
| `apply` | Process matched applications, respecting submission settings |
| `daily` | Discover, match, apply, then send a Telegram digest |
| `digest` | Send a Telegram database summary |
| `stats` | Print counts by job status |
| `prepare` | Time-gated discovery, matching, and runner preparation |
| `assist` | Open an interactive browser flow for manual submission |
| `chat` | Run the Telegram control listener |
| `email` | Process eligible email applications; can send real email when configured |

`--limit` is consumed by application/email processing; it does not limit discovery. Telegram commands include `/menu`, `/status`, `/jobs`, `/applied`, `/skipped`, `/run`, `/search`, `/pause`, `/resume`, `/settings`, and `/help`.

## Matching behavior

A qualifying title starts at **45 points**, and each matching keyword adds **5**, capped at **100**. Excluded title words, unsupported locations, non-target titles, and enabled sponsorship/citizenship exclusion patterns return zero. Jobs meeting `min_score` enter the matched queue. This is a heuristic relevance score, not a probability of getting an interview or a determination of legal eligibility.

## Submission and current limitations

- Start in dry-run mode and inspect local screenshots and logs before enabling submissions. Live form behavior varies across employers and ATS changes.
- Unknown required answers may require review. The public version also leaves prior-employment questions for review instead of embedding a particular applicant's employment history.
- Some answer behavior is heuristic: salary handling includes a default floor when the profile value is absent, demographic fields attempt a decline response, and select controls can vary. Review the actual answers before live use.
- CAPTCHA, unsupported widgets, and bot protection can interrupt a run. There is no guarantee that every form or site is supported.
- Optional AI integrations require valid provider credentials and model availability. No custom model training or fine-tuning is included.
- An empty dashboard displays a notice until application records exist. The preview image is illustrative and is not a bundled live database.
- This release was checked with offline CLI/import, configuration, and matching smoke checks. Live submissions, provider calls, SMTP delivery, and external job boards were not exercised as part of publication.

## Local data and deployment

Keep `.env`, `config/profile.yaml`, Word application documents, resumes, database files, generated letters, and screenshots private. The repository ignores these paths. Do not commit your runtime database to a public repository: it can contain application details and generated letters.

The included Dockerfile runs `python -m jobbot daily` and uses `/data/jobbot.sqlite`. Supply your private profile, resume, optional documents, and secrets at runtime. Mount persistent storage at `/data`; the resume path must match your mounted files. `.dockerignore` excludes local secrets and runtime data from the build context. The base image's Playwright version and the installed dependency version must match; align them before deploying.

For recurring local runs, use your operating system scheduler to invoke the desired CLI command from the repository directory. No active application schedule or database-upload workflow is included in this public edition.

## Repository layout

```text
config/                 Anonymous profile example, settings, company boards
src/jobbot/             Discovery, matching, browser automation, dashboard,
                        document generation, Telegram, email, SQLite
jobbot/                 Root-level module launcher shim
docs/images/            Sample-data dashboard preview
data/logs/.gitkeep      Placeholder; runtime records stay local
.env.example            Empty credential names
Dockerfile              Container entry point
requirements.txt        Python dependencies
```

## Development

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m compileall -q src/jobbot jobbot
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m jobbot --help
```

Use a separate local database via `JOBBOT_DB` when developing. Reproduce form issues in dry-run mode and remove personal information from any shared logs or screenshots. Improvements are welcome through issues and pull requests; include reproducible steps and the affected ATS platform.

projects.readme:
# GenAI LangChat Agent

LangChat is a document workspace for finding relevant excerpts and asking a model to answer with cited context. Add TXT, Markdown, or CSV files, then search them in the browser or send selected passages to local Ollama or OpenRouter.

**[Open LangChat on Vercel](https://genai-langchat-agent.vercel.app)**

## Product gallery

| Desktop workspace | Sample library |
| --- | --- |
| ![Workspace with empty library and prompt examples](docs/screenshots/01-workspace.png) | ![Workspace with sample documents loaded](docs/screenshots/02-source-library.png) |

| Cited search | Model settings |
| --- | --- |
| ![Search result with expanded source excerpt](docs/screenshots/03-cited-search.png) | ![Dialog for OpenRouter credentials and model ID](docs/screenshots/04-model-settings.png) |

[See the mobile upload and cited search screenshot](docs/screenshots/05-mobile-upload-search.png).

## Choose a mode

| Mode | Where it runs | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source search | Browser | Ranked excerpts you can expand and read, without a model or key |
| Local Ollama | Local LangChat server | Generated answers using your installed model and the retrieved excerpts |
| OpenRouter | Local server or Vercel | Generated answers using your OpenRouter account and chosen model |

Use **Load sample documents** or pick one of the example prompts to try a search. Upload your own files via **Add documents**. The library supports up to 20 nonempty files, at most 1 MB per file. **New chat** clears the thread and keeps the currently loaded documents. Reloading the page resets the tab, including the credential entered in Settings.

## Run locally

Use Node.js 24 for the local server and Python 3.10+ if you want the CLI.

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open [localhost:4173](http://127.0.0.1:4173). Source search is ready immediately. For Ollama, start the local service and install a model if it is not already installed.

```sh
ollama pull llama3.2
```

Select **Local Ollama** in the composer. The server defaults to `llama3.2:latest` and connects to `127.0.0.1:11434`. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set `OLLAMA_MODEL` to use a different installed model.

For OpenRouter, enter a key and optional model ID in **Settings**. For local CLI use, store your key as `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in the ignored `.env` file. The default model is `openrouter/free`. Model availability, account charges, and provider rate limits vary. Keep management keys separate from application keys.

The hosted site requires each OpenRouter user to supply their own credential. The key stays in page memory and passes through the HTTPS LangChat endpoint to OpenRouter. The Vercel deployment supports browser search and OpenRouter. Local Ollama runs through the local server.

## Python CLI

Keep the local Node server running for model requests.

```sh
python -m src.agent_cli --prompt "Explain retrieval-augmented generation."
python -m src.agent_cli --interactive
python -m src.agent_cli --provider openrouter --prompt "Explain lexical search."
python -m src.agent_cli --time UTC
```

The CLI shares the model gateway and retains a bounded conversation history in interactive mode. It can look up IANA timezones directly and uses the Python standard library. Install `tzdata` if your OS does not provide an IANA database.

## Retrieval and design

Uploads are read in the browser. The retrieval module splits text into overlapping passages, scores token matches, and returns the three strongest excerpts. Source search displays the passages directly. Model modes send the question and selected excerpts to the provider, using numbered labels that correspond to the expandable sources. Lexical matching can miss paraphrases, and model citations should be checked against the excerpts.

The interface uses a charcoal canvas, olive surfaces, and a citron accent for actions and focus. Color tokens are defined in [web/style.css](web/style.css). At narrow widths, the source library moves above the conversation, and the inputs and cited excerpts remain accessible on a single column.

## Verification

```sh
npm test
npx playwright install chromium
npx playwright test
python -m pip install -r test_requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
```

The Node tests cover retrieval, provider requests, missing credentials, hosted access restrictions, and upstream failures. The browser tests cover the desktop workspace, sample documents, source citations, reset, mobile upload and removal, and request errors. They also regenerate the gallery from the running application. OpenRouter requests are mocked in the Node suite.

## Deployment

Vercel serves `web/` and exposes the Node function at `/api/chat`. Import this repository into Vercel to build another deployment. The local server and CLI run separately on your computer. Keep `.env` and credentials out of Git.

No license has been selected for this repository.

projects.description: Hands-on PyTorch notebooks for generative AI across text, image diffusion, video prediction, masked vision, speech synthesis, symbolic music, and 3D point clouds. Includes a unified inference hub, optional pretrained examples, and illustrated documentation.
projects.readme:
# GenAI - Multimodal Generation Lab

**Build and explore generative AI across text, images, video, vision, speech, music, and 3D with hands-on PyTorch notebooks.**

![Class-conditional sneaker images generated by the project's diffusion model](assets/project-preview.png)

*Actual saved output from the image diffusion notebook: eight Fashion-MNIST sneaker samples generated from noise.*

This educational project walks through seven generative modeling workflows, from preparing data and implementing an architecture to training, sampling, and inspecting results. It includes a combined master notebook, individual notebooks for focused study, and optional pretrained inference examples. The master notebook also exposes a small `MultiModalHub` dispatcher for calling the trained generators through one interface.

The emphasis is understanding how models learn. These are compact teaching implementations with limited datasets and training budgets. The seven workflows cover different modalities; the project does not train a single jointly aligned multimodal foundation model.

## Notebook guide

| Modality | Notebook | Architecture and objective | Data and output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text | [01_Text_GPT.ipynb](01_Text_GPT.ipynb) | Character-level GPT with causal self-attention and next-token cross-entropy | Tiny Shakespeare → sampled text continuations |
| Image | [02_Image_Diffusion.ipynb](02_Image_Diffusion.ipynb) | Class-conditional UNet DDPM, noise-prediction MSE, classifier-free guidance | Fashion-MNIST → 28 × 28 grayscale garment images |
| Video | [03_Video_FramePrediction.ipynb](03_Video_FramePrediction.ipynb) | ConvLSTM sequence prediction with pixel MSE and teacher forcing | Moving sequences constructed from MNIST → future frames |
| Vision | [04_Vision_MaskedImageModeling.ipynb](04_Vision_MaskedImageModeling.ipynb) | Masked autoencoder with reconstruction loss on hidden patches | CIFAR-10 → reconstructed missing image regions |
| Speech | [05_Speech_TextToSpeech.ipynb](05_Speech_TextToSpeech.ipynb) | Tacotron-style text-to-mel network with location-sensitive attention, mel and stop-token losses | Small CMU ARCTIC speaker subset → speech with Griffin–Lim waveform reconstruction |
| Music | [06_Music_SymbolicGeneration.ipynb](06_Music_SymbolicGeneration.ipynb) | GPT over note/rest/duration events with next-event prediction | Bach chorales from music21 → monophonic melodies, piano rolls, and synthesized audio |
| 3D | [07_3D_PointCloudGeneration.ipynb](07_3D_PointCloudGeneration.ipynb) | Class-conditional PointNet-style VAE with Chamfer distance and KL regularization | Procedural sphere, cube, cone, cylinder, and torus → 512-point shapes |

**Start with the complete walkthrough:** [Multi-Modal_Generative_AI_Master_Notebook.ipynb](Multi-Modal_Generative_AI_Master_Notebook.ipynb).

## What you will learn

- Prepare text vocabularies, image transforms, video sequences, mel spectrograms, music events, and unordered point sets.
- Implement attention, autoregressive decoding, diffusion denoising, recurrent visual prediction, masked reconstruction, and variational sampling.
- Match each modality to a suitable loss and training strategy.
- Use checkpoints, loss plots, sample visualizations, and notebook audio playback to inspect behavior.
- Explore temperature/top-k sampling, diffusion guidance, image masking ratios, and conditional 3D generation.
- Compare a small model trained from scratch with optional pretrained inference paths.

## Setup and first run

Use an isolated Python environment supported by the PyTorch packages you install. A CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU is recommended for training. CPU execution is supported by the notebook device-selection logic but can take substantially longer.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/GenAI-Multimodal-Generation-Lab.git
cd GenAI-Multimodal-Generation-Lab
python -m venv .venv
```

Activate the environment:

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

```bash
# macOS / Linux
source .venv/bin/activate
```

Install a compatible `torch`, `torchvision`, and `torchaudio` set using the [official PyTorch installation selector](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/), choosing the build appropriate to your platform and GPU. Then install the remaining notebook dependencies:

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m jupyter lab
```

1. Open the master notebook for the full sequence, or select an individual modality notebook.
2. Select the kernel for your environment and run the global setup cells first.
3. Run the remaining cells in order. In the master notebook, later sections reuse earlier definitions, including GPT for symbolic music.
4. Allow dataset downloads on the first run. Keep the working directory at the repository root so relative paths resolve consistently.
5. Train the model before running its generation/demo cells. Adjust the step/epoch settings to your compute budget.

The setup cells also install `music21`, `soundfile`, and `imageio`. Optional pretrained paths may install additional packages and download model weights. Dependencies in `requirements.txt` are unpinned starting requirements, not a tested environment lockfile.

## Unified inference hub

After running the relevant training and definition cells in the master notebook, Section 8 constructs `hub` with seven modality routes:

```python
hub.generate("text", "ROMEO:", max_new_tokens=200)
hub.generate("image", "Sneaker", n_samples=4)
hub.generate("speech", "Hello from the multimodal notebook.")
hub.generate("3d", "sphere", n_samples=1)
```

The remaining routes are `video`, `vision`, and `music`; their inputs are context-frame tensors, image tensors, and music seed events respectively. Output types follow each notebook's generator. The hub is an in-memory dispatcher over initialized models, rather than an independently packaged service. The final section includes an illustrative Gradio UI example for text and image generation; a deployed application is not included.

## Project results gallery

The images below are extracted from existing notebook outputs. They illustrate a saved run and are not newly measured benchmarks.

### Video continuation

![Saved Moving-MNIST frame prediction output](assets/video-prediction.png)

ConvLSTM predictions illustrate how a recurrent visual model continues simple moving-digit sequences.

### Masked image reconstruction

![Original, masked, and reconstructed CIFAR-10 images](assets/masked-reconstruction.png)

The vision notebook compares an input image, its masked version, and the reconstructed image.

### Conditional 3D shapes

![Generated point clouds for five primitive shape classes](assets/point-clouds.png)

The 3D notebook samples class-conditioned point clouds from the VAE latent space.

## Optional pretrained paths

The notebooks include optional examples for GPT-2, Stable Diffusion, pretrained video diffusion, ViT-MAE, SpeechT5 with HiFi-GAN, MusicGen, and Shap-E. These paths are controlled by notebook flags and are off by default. Inspect each example before enabling it: model downloads, hardware requirements, dependencies, access conditions, and model licenses differ.

## Data, generated files, and repository layout

```text
.
├── README.md
├── requirements.txt
├── assets/                       # Result images used in this README
├── 01_Text_GPT.ipynb
├── 02_Image_Diffusion.ipynb
├── 03_Video_FramePrediction.ipynb
├── 04_Vision_MaskedImageModeling.ipynb
├── 05_Speech_TextToSpeech.ipynb
├── 06_Music_SymbolicGeneration.ipynb
├── 07_3D_PointCloudGeneration.ipynb
└── Multi-Modal_Generative_AI_Master_Notebook.ipynb
```

Datasets are downloaded or constructed by notebook cells. Runtime directories such as `data/`, `checkpoints/`, and `outputs/` are excluded from this public source snapshot. Existing inline notebook plots and audio are retained. Downloaded datasets and pretrained weights remain subject to their respective providers' terms.

## Compute, limitations, and reproducibility

The notebook narrative reports short training runs calibrated on an RTX 2060 with 6 GB VRAM. Treat those timings as author-reported examples, not guarantees: hardware, package versions, download time, and runtime configuration affect results. The publication work did not rerun training or independently verify those timings.

Expect limited long-range coherence in tiny text models, low-resolution diffusion samples, blur in video predictions, approximate masked-image reconstruction, and low-fidelity speech from short training and Griffin–Lim inversion. Music is monophonic with simple synthesized timbre. The 3D output is a point cloud with a fixed point count, not a textured mesh.

For repeatable experiments, record your package versions, random seed, device, dataset subset, training settings, and checkpoint. The notebooks provide seed and checkpoint helpers, but exact numerical agreement across devices is not guaranteed.

## Troubleshooting

- **GPU is not detected:** check `torch.cuda.is_available()` and install the appropriate PyTorch build for your platform and driver.
- **Missing variables or models:** restart the kernel and execute the notebook from its setup cells in order.
- **Out of GPU memory:** reduce batch size or model size and leave unused pretrained paths disabled.
- **Dataset download fails:** verify connectivity and write access to `data/`, then rerun the preparation cell.
- **Speech package/backend errors:** keep PyTorch-family versions compatible; the notebook uses `soundfile` for waveform reading to avoid relying on an optional torchaudio decoding backend.

## Extending the project

Possible next steps include larger datasets, longer training, polyphonic music encoding, neural speech vocoders, improved video generation objectives, point-cloud diffusion, and cross-modal conditioning. The master notebook discusses LoRA, quantization, and UI integration as extension ideas; these are not complete production features in this repository.

## Author and reuse

Maintained by [Vamshi Krishna Adam](https://github.com/vams2krish). Questions and reproducible bug reports can be shared through this repository's Issues tab. Include the notebook name, runtime versions, device, and relevant error message.

No project license has been selected in this publication. Public visibility alone does not grant an open-source license. Dataset, model, and dependency licenses apply separately.

projects.readme:
# GenAI Startup Brief Agent · Brief Studio

**[Open live web research](https://genai-startup-brief-agent.vercel.app/)**

Turn an early startup idea into a structured planning brief. The hosted app searches Tavily for evidence relevant to your idea and adds a linked source list. Local Ollama mode creates a separate model-generated draft.

![Brief Studio desktop workspace and photographed startup examples](docs/screenshots/07-real-examples.png)

## Features

- Enter an idea and optional audience, budget, or launch constraints, or prefill the form with an example.
- Generate a brief covering customers, competition, business model, go-to-market, financial assumptions, and risks. The local prompt requests 15 sections.
- Copy the brief or download Markdown. A failed request keeps the previous brief available.
- Generate a brief from the terminal or use the general chat CLI.

## Real examples and screenshots

Explore [Airbnb’s first hosted stays](https://news.airbnb.com/airbnb-celebrates-half-a-billion-guest-arrivals) and [Buffer’s landing-page test](https://buffer.com/resources/idea-to-paying-customers-in-7-weeks-how-we-did-it/). Each case includes an experiment you can adapt and a starter idea you can load into the form.

[Desktop gallery](docs/screenshots/07-real-examples.png) · [Loaded example brief](docs/screenshots/08-loaded-example.png) · [Mobile gallery](docs/screenshots/09-mobile-examples.png)

Illustrative photography from Unsplash: [living room](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1600210492486-724fe5c67fb0) and [laptop workspace](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1516321318423-f06f85e504b3).

## Run with local Ollama

Prerequisites: Python 3.10+, Node.js 22+, npm, and a running Ollama instance. From the repository root on Windows:

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt -r test_requirements.txt
npm --prefix ui ci
ollama pull llama3.2:latest
npm --prefix ui start
```

On macOS or Linux, use `.venv/bin/python` instead. Open [127.0.0.1:3000](http://127.0.0.1:3000). Start `ollama serve` if Ollama is not running. Pull the exact model tag you intend to use. Cloud model tags require Ollama account access and can send prompts off-device.

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | Model endpoint; defaults to `http://localhost:11434`. |
| `OLLAMA_MODEL_LIST_RETRIES` | Availability attempts; default 5. |
| `OLLAMA_MODEL_LIST_RETRY_SLEEP_SECONDS` | Delay between attempts; default 1 second. |
| `SKIP_OLLAMA_MODEL_VALIDATION` | Set to 1 to skip model availability validation. |
| `PORT` | Local web port; default 3000. |
| `PYTHON_EXEC` | Override the Python interpreter used by Express. |

Use `.env.example` for Python settings. Set Node variables in the shell that starts the server.

## CLI

With the environment active:

```powershell
python src/startup_agent_cli.py --idea "A scheduling assistant for independent fitness coaches"
python src/agent_cli.py --prompt "Explain product-market fit"
python src/agent_cli.py --interactive
```

Interactive chat includes the latest six exchanges. Type `exit` or `quit` to end.

## Architecture and tests

Set the optional TAVILY_API_KEY server environment variable in Vercel to use your Tavily account quota. Shared access is used by default. Vercel serves the interface from `ui/public`. Locally, the loopback Express server validates the request and invokes the Python CLI with a timeout. The CLI renders `agent_startup.yaml`, calls Ollama through LangChain, and prints response text. The browser displays output as text and exports Markdown. Market claims and financial assumptions need independent verification.

See the [UI documentation](ui/README_UI.md) for design tokens. Run `python -m pytest -q` and `node --check ui/server.js` for local checks. No license has been selected.
