projects.description: Local, free/open-source research paper reader with AI-powered breakdowns, synthesis, and spaced repetition.
projects.readme: # ResearchPal **Read the whole document. Understand the evidence. Turn what you learn into an explanation.** ResearchPal is a local-first reading and research workspace for desktop and mobile browsers. Import PDF, DOCX, Markdown or text; read its complete extracted source; listen to narration; generate study material; and create an editable, narrated video explainer. Version **0.2.1** adds uninstall options to the Windows desktop app. It builds on task-specific model connections, automatic Ollama storage discovery, a full Markdown reader, source audio exports, Explainer Studio and a responsive interface. ![ResearchPal full document reader and narration controls](docs/images/live/reader.png) *Screenshots use an illustrative campus shade study in a separate demo library on the installed Windows backend. Live model calls stay on the machine. No audio was generated or played during this run.* [Problem](#the-problem) · [Features](#features) · [Setup](#quick-start) · [Models](#models-and-connections) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Verification](#verification) · [Limitations](#limitations) ## The problem Understanding a research paper means connecting its problem, methods, assumptions, equations, evaluation conditions and limitations. Reading several papers adds the challenge of remembering which source supports which claim. Conventional workflows scatter this work between PDF readers, notes, chat, citations and flashcards. Short summaries can drop the conditions and qualifications that give a finding meaning. ResearchPal combines these activities while retaining the complete extracted source. Reading does not require generating a summary first. The application serves students learning technical literature, researchers organizing evidence, engineers comparing methods, and independent learners building a review routine. Generated output is an aid to investigation, not independent scientific verification. ## The end-to-end workflow 1. **Connect:** discover local/cloud models in Settings and choose a provider/model for each task. 2. **Import:** add a document. Import does not automatically start text-generation or embedding jobs; configured OCR can run during PDF extraction. 3. **Read:** explore full Markdown, follow its outline, inspect raw source or download the `.md` file. 4. **Listen:** use a device voice, or explicitly generate exported narration of every extracted source part. 5. **Study:** generate anatomy, explanations, formulas, claims, glossary terms and flashcards; check them against the source. 6. **Question:** ask about one paper, compare papers, synthesize evidence or investigate with web research. 7. **Explain:** generate or write a storyboard, edit every scene, then choose local slides, generated images or generated motion. 8. **Reuse:** download narrated MP4, complete MP3, source Markdown, notes, citations or Anki TSV, and return for spaced review. ## Features | Area | What is available | | --- | --- | | Library | PDF/DOCX/Markdown/text, favorites, tags, collections and immediate source reading. | | Markdown reader | Full extracted document, outline, tables, lists, code, math, raw source and download; sanitized HTML. | | Full narration | Device voices with pause/resume, speed and part controls; exported MP3 parts, playlist and combined full-document MP3. | | Paper anatomy | Title/Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Experimental Setup, Results, Related Work, Discussion, Conclusion, References, Appendix. | | Section analysis | Long sections are visited in bounded parts rather than silently clipping tails; original headings are retained. | | Evidence | Formulas, figures/tables/code, claim/evidence/assumption/limitation cards and generated first-principles breakdowns. | | Learning | Mind maps, diagrams, glossary, mental models, section notes, human-written notes and FSRS flashcards. | | Original PDF | PDF.js reading, highlights and image-region questions through the selected vision model. | | Research | Retrieved paper questions, synthesis/critique, 2–4-paper comparison, bounded web search/fetch research. | | Explainer Studio | Document/text → editable storyboard → narrated H.264/AAC MP4 with slides, images or motion. | | Connections | Separate text, vision, embedding, image, video, speech and OCR routes; discovery or manual IDs/URLs. | | Local storage | Structural Ollama folder discovery, manual override and optional desktop-managed Ollama startup. | | Jobs | Persisted progress/results for narration, storyboards, video and reindexing; visible interruption without paid resubmission. | | Interface | Light/dark themes, focused navigation, responsive reading and mobile bottom navigation. | | Exports | Source Markdown, study notes, BibTeX, Anki TSV, audio and video. | ### Product showcase **Library.** Import a document and open the extracted source before generating study notes. ![ResearchPal live demo library](docs/images/live/library.png) **Study mode.** Navigate generated sections while keeping extracted text available for checking details. ![Study view with paper anatomy and original Methods text](docs/images/live/study.png) **Ask This Paper.** The local model retrieved the source and correctly answered that the measured difference was 8 °C. ![Live answer grounded in the imported document](docs/images/live/question.png) **Explainer Studio.** Generate a storyboard with the local model and edit its scene text before rendering. ![Editable storyboard generated with Ollama](docs/images/live/studio.png) **Model settings.** Assign generation and embeddings separately using the installed Ollama service. ![Separate text and embedding model settings](docs/images/live/models.png) ### Mobile reading The responsive browser/PWA interface is the tested mobile path. Separate SwiftUI source under `ios-native/` remains experimental and uncompiled, without browser feature parity. ## Quick start ### Requirements Python 3.11, Git and a modern browser are the documented development baseline. Local generation/embeddings require Ollama with models installed; cloud features need the selected provider's credentials. Node.js/npm is needed only for Electron development/packaging. Hardware requirements depend on the models; no benchmarked minimum is published. ### Windows PowerShell ```powershell git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/ResearchPal.git cd ResearchPal py -3.11 -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt Copy-Item .env.example .env .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m uvicorn server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8501 ``` ### macOS / Linux ```bash git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/ResearchPal.git cd ResearchPal python3.11 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt cp .env.example .env .venv/bin/python -m uvicorn server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8501 ``` Open [the local app](http://127.0.0.1:8501) and configure Settings. [Interactive API docs](http://127.0.0.1:8501/docs) come from FastAPI. The frontend has no separate build/dev server. Reading text documents needs no model; analysis, indexing and media require their task routes. ### Desktop and installer After Python setup: ```bash cd desktop npm install npm start ``` The shell chooses an available loopback port and verifies its backend's instance identity. It does not assume a fixed-port server belongs to this app. Build the Windows installer from the repository root: ```powershell .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install pyinstaller cd desktop npm install npm run dist ``` Output: `desktop/dist/ResearchPal Setup 0.2.1.exe`. PyInstaller bundles Python and FFmpeg; electron-builder creates the installer. Model weights and OCR inference runtimes are not bundled. Application data stays outside the executable. Choosing a different existing library folder in desktop Settings requires restart and does not copy the old library automatically. To remove the Windows desktop app, open **Settings → Desktop app → Uninstall ResearchPal**. ResearchPal asks before opening the standard uninstaller. **Windows Installed apps** is available in the same panel as a fallback. The library is stored separately. macOS scripts exist, but macOS packaging/native iOS compilation are not verified by this Windows workflow. ## Models and connections ![Task-specific model configuration](docs/images/researchpal-settings.png) Settings distinguishes a **service connection** from the **model used for a task**. A folder path is not a service URL; model storage belongs to the serving application. | Connection | Tasks | Configuration | | --- | --- | --- | | Ollama | Text, vision, embeddings | Service URL, model IDs, optional storage folder for app-managed startup. | | Gemini | Text, vision | Key and available model ID. | | OpenRouter | Text, vision, embeddings, images, video, speech | Key, base URL, capability-appropriate model IDs; dedicated image/video discovery. | | Compatible API | Text, vision, embeddings, images, video, speech | User URL/key; server must implement each selected protocol. | | ComfyUI | Images, video | Service, API-format workflow, positive prompt node/input, optional checkpoint. | | Automatic1111 | Images | WebUI with `--api`, service URL, checkpoint. | | Unlimited-OCR 2 | OCR | Separate upstream SGLang server, `/v1` URL and served model ID. | | Baidu cloud OCR | OCR | API/secret keys and OCR service access; separate from Unlimited-OCR. | | Device speech | Immediate reading | Device/browser voice; no server audio export. | | Windows speech | Offline audio/video export | Installed voice; blank model field selects its default. | | Edge speech | Online audio/video export | Neural voice ID or default. | Nano Banana and Seedance are model families, not universal API identifiers. Discover or enter the exact models offered by the provider/account; not every model supports every modality. ### Moving Ollama models 1. Open **Settings → Ollama → Find model folders automatically**. 2. Optionally enter a search folder/drive. Discovery checks for `manifests`/`blobs`, skips dependency/system directories and reports search limits. 3. Select a location or enter a manual path, then Save. 4. If no service runs, desktop can start Ollama with this folder. Otherwise restart the external service with updated `OLLAMA_MODELS`; ResearchPal does not take it over. 5. Discover service model IDs and assign task models. No machine-specific model directory is committed in source. Windows discovery reads current user environment settings rather than only an inherited desktop environment. ComfyUI/Automatic1111 checkpoint folders remain server-owned. ### Cloud use and costs Studio displays selected task providers/models before Generate. Image/video modes request one visual generation per scene; long narration needs multiple speech calls. Jobs start only on explicit actions. The UI disables silent cross-provider fallback; restart does not resubmit paid jobs automatically. Provider pricing, quota, access and parameters are external constraints. Discovery does not prove generation access for every listed model. See [the integration guide](docs/providers.md) for endpoint contracts and upstream references. ## Reading, narration and OCR Source narration uses extracted words, removes visual markup/file paths, visits all bounded parts and creates MP3 parts, a playlist and a combined MP3. The older PDF narration action is labelled **study summary** to distinguish it from full source narration. Spoken interpretation of mathematics, tables and layout depends on extraction and voice quality. Automatic OCR detects image pages with little readable text. Always OCR parses the full PDF; Off accepts partial native extraction. Unlimited-OCR sends ordered page images to SGLang and checks page markers/output-budget completion. Baidu cloud OCR handles pages individually and reports quota/service errors. There is no fixed application page-count cutoff. Memory, payload size, token budgets and inference time still bound practical workloads. Unlimited-OCR is a separate GPU service; its upstream example uses an A800 with 80 GB memory. Installing ResearchPal does not install those weights or make a small GPU sufficient. See [upstream setup](https://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR). DOCX retains text and recognized headings, not complete Word layout, embedded media or rich table structure. Convert `.doc` to `.docx` first. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD A[PDF / DOCX / Markdown / text] --> B[Extract source; optional OCR] B --> C[SQLite library and full reader] C --> D[Device speech / full-source audio export] C --> E[Explicit study generation and retrieval] C --> F[Editable Studio storyboard] F --> G[Local slides / provider images / provider video] G --> H[Speech and local FFmpeg assembly] H --> I[Downloadable narrated MP4] J[Connections and capability routes] --> D J --> E J --> F ``` | Layer | Implementation | | --- | --- | | Interface | HTML/CSS/JS modules, Marked/DOMPurify, responsive desktop/mobile views. | | API | FastAPI/Uvicorn, source imports, connections, jobs/progress. | | Data | SQLite, documents, connection settings, job manifests and local media. | | Models | Ollama/Gemini/OpenRouter/compatible APIs, separate capability routes. | | Retrieval | Configurable embeddings in SQLite BLOBs; NumPy cosine ranking. | | Parsing | PyMuPDF4LLM/PyMuPDF, DOCX XML extraction, optional OCR servers. | | Media | Device speech, Windows SAPI, Edge/cloud speech, Pillow, FFmpeg H.264/AAC. | | Learning | FSRS, KaTeX, PDF.js, Mermaid, Markmap/D3; DDGS/Requests/BeautifulSoup research. | | Distribution | Electron, PyInstaller, Windows NSIS installer. | ### Repository map ```text ResearchPal/ ├── server.py # API and analysis queue ├── core/ │ ├── providers.py # Connections, discovery and task routing │ ├── model_storage.py # Ollama folder discovery │ ├── documents.py # Extraction and OCR │ ├── jobs.py # Persisted jobs and bounded workers │ ├── media.py # Narration, storyboards, image/video adapters │ ├── pipeline.py # Anatomy and research analysis │ ├── vectorstore.py # Source chunks and semantic search │ └── ... # SQLite, audio, exports, review, research ├── static/ # Shared desktop/mobile interface ├── assets/ # Bundled renderers and icons ├── desktop/ # Electron and installer build ├── ios-native/ # Experimental native client ├── tests/ # Regression/API tests ├── scripts/smoke_workspace.py # Browser/API/real-media test └── docs/ # Guide, screenshots, verification ``` ## Configuration, data and privacy Settings saves `connections.json` in the active data directory. Keys remain server-side, are omitted from responses and never appear in media URLs. Blank inputs preserve stored keys. Local credentials are plaintext files protected by filesystem permissions, not an encrypted vault. `.env` supplies initial/default `PRIMARY_LLM`, Gemini settings, Ollama host/text/vision/embedding settings and `OLLAMA_NUM_CTX`. Saved routes control new jobs. `OCE_DATA_DIR` overrides storage; `OCE_PORT` controls the standalone entry point. Desktop manages its available port and optional library folder. Storage defaults: `data/` in a source checkout; `%LOCALAPPDATA%/ResearchPal` on installed Windows; `~/Library/Application Support/ResearchPal` on frozen macOS; `~/.researchpal` on other frozen systems. Back up with the app stopped before moving data. Reindex after any embedding-model change, including same-dimension changes. Local-first does not mean offline-only. Cloud models receive source/prompts; OCR servers receive page images; web research contacts external services; Edg

projects.readme:
# SkullBot — Good writing has good bones.

A writing studio for ideas, clearer drafts, source review, and academic documents. **Chat, paraphrase, proofread, summarize, organize citations, format APA papers, and inspect similarity in one workspace.**

[Open the private app](https://skullbot-writing-lab.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site) · [Run locally](#run-locally) · [Product showcases](#product-showcases-with-real-examples) · [Architecture](docs/detection/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Verification](docs/detection/VERIFICATION.md)

[![Checks](https://github.com/vams2krish/SkullBot-GenAI-Writing-Studio/actions/workflows/check.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/vams2krish/SkullBot-GenAI-Writing-Studio/actions/workflows/check.yml)

![SkullBot Chat producing leadership themes and evidence placeholders](docs/showcase/01-chat.jpg)

The hosted app is owner-private; this source repository is public. The optional Python detection service currently runs **locally**, by the owner's choice. Hosted fingerprint matching works without it; hosted neural and semantic results accurately show unavailable until a reachable backend is connected.

## Everything in the workspace

| Feature | What you can do | How it runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **SkullBot Chat** | Ask questions, develop outlines, follow up, copy/regenerate answers, stop generation, start a new chat | OpenRouter; optional device chat storage |
| **Paraphraser** | Standard, Fluency, Humanize, Formal, Academic, Simple, Creative; rewrite intensity 0–100 | OpenRouter |
| **Grammar checker & red squiggles** | Review spelling/basic grammar, choose replacements, ignore terms; request an AI grammar pass | Local dictionary/rules plus optional OpenRouter correction |
| **AI humanizer** | Basic/Advanced natural-voice editing, or **Rules (local)** | OpenRouter for Basic/Advanced; deterministic rules for local mode |
| **TurnitOFF** | Apply inspectable rules, protect terms/math/code/citations, constrain word growth, inspect every edit | Browser-local, zero generative AI; 27 bundled rules |
| **Document processing** | Edit eligible prose/runs/comments in documents and mixed ZIPs while auditing preservation | Local parsers, XML checks and archive limits |
| **ZipPy lab** | Compare actual gzip size, byte entropy, sentence variation and 3/4/5-gram overlap | Descriptive local measurements |
| **Summarizer** | Short, Medium, Long, Detailed summaries with length checks | OpenRouter; labeled extractive fallback |
| **Plagiarism checker** | Fingerprint matching, ranked sources, exact highlights, exclusions and opt-in repository comparisons | Local device matching or private Python service |
| **Semantic review** | Find meaning-similar passages using embeddings, with source IDs/offsets | Optional Python model service; separate from exact coverage |
| **AI detector** | Independent experimental transformer indicator, projected sentence highlights and abstention | Optional Python classifier; English baseline, minimum prose length |
| **Citation generator** | Webpage/book/journal APA templates, alphabetical reference library and in-text forms | Manually supplied source metadata |
| **TurnitOFF citation engine** | Explicit source markers, hierarchical subject labels, APA/IEEE/BibTeX/LaTeX/JSON exports | Deterministic; no invented source discovery |
| **APA 7 formatter** | Student/professional metadata, content preview and formatted DOCX | Server-side document generation |
| **Workspace controls** | Copy/download, use result as draft, recent activity, optional saving, clear workspace, responsive navigation | Browser/device storage; no cross-device sync |

## Product showcases with real examples

The screenshots below are fresh captures of the running product using synthetic classroom/test examples. Generated responses are actual observed outputs, not mockups; another model run can differ. Examples demonstrate functionality, not factual correctness or detector accuracy. [Screenshot gallery and provenance](docs/showcase/README.md).

### 1. Turn an assignment into a research conversation

**Use case:** a student needs to plan a 2,500-word case study about a leader across cultures using Yin's method and APA 7.

Try:

> Outline a 2,500-word case study of a leader across cultures using Yin’s method. Give six leadership themes and evidence placeholders. Do not invent sources or interviews.

The observed answer organized a case-study design and named six themes: communication adaptation, power distance, relationship/task-oriented trust, conflict management, motivation/recognition, and change management. Evidence remained explicitly marked as placeholders. Follow up with:

> Turn the outline into a five-step research checklist. Identify which sources and evidence I still need to supply.

Chat supports Markdown answers, follow-ups, copy, regenerate, stop/retry, and optional device storage. It does not browse the web or verify references. Prompted length goals are not hard guarantees.

### 2. Rephrase an academic draft

Choose **Paraphraser → Academic** and adjust rewrite intensity.

**Input used in the live showcase:**

> Our team studied how leaders work across cultures. We compared interview notes with public documents and considered alternative explanations before drawing conclusions.

**Observed output:**

> We examined how leaders operate across cultures by comparing interview notes with public documents and considering alternative explanations before drawing conclusions.

![Academic paraphrasing with original text and observed rewrite](docs/showcase/02-paraphraser.jpg)

The other modes offer different registers. Intensity zero is preserved as zero; it requests minimal editing rather than disabling the model. Review meaning, nuance, quotations and attribution after every rewrite.

### 3. Catch errors with red squiggles

Paste:

```text
i recieve teh report and keep seperate notes. The researcher have evidence.
```

Red wavy underlines identify spelling/basic grammar issues in the editor. Open a suggestion to replace a span or ignore a term. One live AI pass returned the following (it also changed the tense, so review the intended time frame):

```text
I received the report and kept separate notes. The researcher has evidence.
```

![Grammar corrections and red proofreading underlines](docs/showcase/03-grammar.jpg)

The local pass is deliberately narrower than a complete grammar model. For example, the deterministic grammar function corrects `i recieve teh report and keep seperate notes.` to `I receive the report and keep separate notes.`; broader agreement correction uses the AI pass or targeted editor suggestions.

### 4. Choose model editing or a deterministic Humanizer pass

**Basic / Advanced** request natural-voice editing through OpenRouter. **Rules (local)** uses the same inspectable engine as TurnitOFF.

Actual deterministic example:

```text
Before: Furthermore, we utilize evidence in order to evaluate $E=mc^2$ (Smith, 2024).
After:  Also, we use evidence to evaluate $E=mc^2$ (Smith, 2024).
```

![Humanizer running the local deterministic mode](docs/showcase/04-humanizer.jpg)

The equation and citation are unchanged. `Smith, 2024` is a synthetic preservation-test marker, not a supplied or verified reference. Humanizer editing does not establish detector evasion.

### 5. Condense a long research draft

Use **Summarizer → Short / Medium / Long / Detailed**. The result labels whether it came from AI assistance or an extractive fallback.

The fresh screenshot uses a 92-word classroom-methodology draft. Its observed Short result was: “This case study examines cross-cultural leadership without stereotypes, using verified evidence and comparing observed patterns against rival explanations.”

A previous live QA run used the same synthetic 2,836-word cross-cultural leadership research-plan draft:

| Mode | Target words | Observed words | Method |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Short | 567 | 558 | AI-assisted |
| Medium | 1,134 | 1,128 | Labeled extractive fallback |
| Long | 1,702 | 1,702 | Labeled extractive fallback |
| Detailed | 2,269 | 2,269 | Labeled extractive fallback |

![Summarizer showing a condensed classroom example](docs/showcase/05-summarizer.jpg)

These are individual runs, not universal length or quality guarantees. Out-of-budget or truncated model summaries trigger a labeled fallback built from intact original sentences. See the [original QA report](docs/QA-REPORT.md).

### 6. Make protected, reviewable edits with TurnitOFF

TurnitOFF v1.0.0 is an English literal-rule engine with **27 downloadable rules**, not an LLM paraphraser.

The example above produces three logged edits—`in order to → to`, `utilize → use`, `Furthermore, → Also,`—and preserves two protected spans. Its rule-pass count decreases from **11 to 9 words**.

![TurnitOFF protected editing and change audit](docs/showcase/06-turnitoff.jpg)

Controls include technical fidelity, zero expansion, discourse/concision switches, protected terms and custom literal JSON rules. Higher fidelity permits fewer authored rules; it is not a learned probability. Zero expansion means the word count cannot increase, not that it stays exactly equal.

For example, protect `utilize` and transform:

```text
We utilize evidence in order to learn.
→ We utilize evidence to learn.
```

An additional custom rule can use this schema:

```json
[{"id":"team-01","from":"prior to","to":"before","stage":"lexical","alignment":99}]
```

Duplicate IDs, empty/multiline phrases, malformed JSON and invalid alignment values are rejected. Math, fenced/inline code, citations, URLs, quotes, numbers and user-protected terms are conservatively masked. Review all edits for meaning. There is no verified detector bypass, semantic-equivalence certification, watermark removal or 4,000-rule catalog.

### 7. Process documents and code without rewriting executable statements

TurnitOFF's **Documents** tab accepts TXT, Markdown, LaTeX, DOCX, ZIP, JS, JSX, TS, TSX, MJS, CJS and Python.

Actual JavaScript example:

```javascript
// Before: Utilize evidence in order to proceed.
const label = "utilize";

// After: Use evidence to proceed.
const label = "utilize";
```

![Mixed-project ZIP processing with per-file audits](docs/showcase/12-documents.jpg)

JS/TS/Python parsers identify eligible comments and verify the result; strings, executable text, Python docstrings and tool directives remain intact. Beginner / Intermediate / Architect profiles adjust fidelity thresholds; they do not generate new comments.

DOCX processing edits eligible `w:t` run text while checking XML tags/attributes and retaining other package content. Complex/protected paragraphs are skipped conservatively, including protected phrases split across formatting runs. Unsupported binaries and nested ZIPs are preserved, with per-file failures reported. Metadata is preserved.

Limits: **10 MB upload, 500 archive entries, 20 MB per expanded entry, 50 MB total expanded data**. This does not guarantee arbitrary document rendering or semantic fidelity. [Full TurnitOFF audit](docs/TURNITOFF-AUDIT.md).

### 8. Measure text with ZipPy

The **ZipPy lab** compares original and transformed text using actual gzip bytes, UTF-8 byte Shannon entropy, mean sentence length, sentence-length variation, and original/output 3/4/5-gram Jaccard overlap. Measurements can be exported as JSON.

![ZipPy descriptive text measurements](docs/showcase/07-zippy.jpg)

These are descriptive measurements—not language-model perplexity, AI probabilities, a web plagiarism score, or a submission-readiness score. Byte entropy and gzip size depend strongly on text length/content.

### 9. Inspect exact overlap separately from semantic similarity

Paste this same fixture into the submission and a supplied source:

> Culturally responsive leaders listen carefully before making important decisions across national borders.

The hosted fingerprint engine reports **100% exact coverage** for the identical text. Excluding that source and rerunning gives **0%** when no other qualifying source remains. Duplicate/overlapping source matches are unioned rather than double-counted.

The fresh screenshot adds 14 original words after that copied sentence: **12 of 26 eligible words matched (46.15%)**, with the copied span highlighted. The short input correctly receives no AI percentage.

![Similarity report with ranked sources and independent indicators](docs/showcase/08-similarity.jpg)

You can exclude quotations, bibliography, small matches or specific sources. Indexing is off by default. Device sources remain on the device; service sources belong to a credential-scoped tenant repository. Institutional settings control member indexing. Self-overlap and shared tenant text are review leads, not misconduct findings.

A real local embedding smoke test used:

- **Source:** “A cross-cultural leader listens carefully before making important decisions. Respectful communication helps international teams work together effectively.”
- **Submission:** “Leaders working across cultures listen attentively before they make major decisions. International teams collaborate more effectively when communication is respectful.”
- **Observed result:** **0% lexical overlap**, one semantic candidate at **cosine 0.8928** using the configured MiniLM model.

Semantic candidates stay separate from exact coverage. This one fixture is not a paraphrase-detection accuracy benchmark. The product does not search Turnitin, the open web, publisher databases or a licensed academic corpus.

### 10. Run an independent, explicitly experimental AI analysis

The local Python service runs actual pretrained classifier weights. The default English baseline is `fakespot-ai/roberta-base-ai-text-detection-v1`, with selectable Desklib DeBERTa; the observed revision is recorded in the [verification report](docs/detection/VERIFICATION.md).

The refreshed screenshot uses Desklib on a 365-word repeated synthetic fixture: 91.23% thresholded word share. This demonstrates model execution, not accuracy.

![Local classifier-backed AI indicator, explicitly labeled experimental](docs/showcase/09-ai-detector.jpg)

The indicator is the eligible word share in sentences whose projected window-model score meets the configured threshold. It is **not the probability that a person used AI**. Sentence values project overlapping-window scores; they are not independently calibrated sentence probabilities.

- Fewer than 300 eligible prose words: no AI percentage; minimum-length explanation.
- No configured model/service: unavailable, not a fabricated fallback score.
- Unsupported language: the English baseline abstains.
- Exclude a matching source: exact similarity changes independently of the AI result.

Descriptive features and optional reference-LM perplexity are separate signals. No validated modern-LLM false-positive rate, AI-paraphrase accuracy, multilingual AI accuracy or commercial-tool equivalence is claimed. Human review is essential.

### 11. Build references from source records you supply

Enter a book record such as author `Yin, R. K.`, year `2018`, title `Case study research and applications: Design and methods`, publisher `SAGE`.

The current common-source template produces:

```text
Yin, R. K. (2018). Case study research and applications: Design and methods. SAGE.
In-text form: (Yin, 2018)
```

![Citation entry and alphabetical reference library](docs/showcase/10-citations.jpg)

**Find academic sources** searches real Crossref metadata. Try `cross cultural leadership`, select **Multilingual E5 small** for local metadata ranking, then **Add source**. Only your query goes to Crossref; no manuscript is sent. Missing models retain Crossref order. Unsupported source types are omitted from the common-source templates. Relevance ranking does not verify claim support.

Verify the publication and add source-specific details such as edition where required. Templates support webpages, books and journal articles, multiple/group au

projects.name: StoryTime
projects.description: Interactive bedtime stories with OpenRouter, cached ElevenLabs narration, Hugging Face cover art and video, printable PDFs, and local Ollama fallback.
projects.readme:
# StoryTime

**Little stories. Big dreams.** A cozy AI storytelling app for children and the grown-ups who read with them, with cloud AI and local fallbacks.

StoryTime turns a child's favorite character into personalized bedtime stories, interactive adventures, printable books, and narrated reading sessions. It uses **OpenRouter** for story text, **ElevenLabs** for speech, and **Hugging Face Inference Providers** for cover art and short story videos. Ollama, Automatic1111, and device voices or Kokoro provide local fallbacks.

![StoryTime home screen with a moonlit cottage illustration](docs/images/demo-home.jpg)

## Product showcase

The gallery follows Mira, a fictional demo hero who loves lavender and foxes.

| My Little Heroes | Create an adventure |
| --- | --- |
| ![Mira's saved hero profile](docs/images/demo-heroes.jpg) | ![Story creation form with the forest theme and interactive mode selected](docs/images/demo-create.jpg) |
| Save a character and start a new story from their profile. | Pick a theme and give the adventure a small wish. |

| Story reader | Reading rewards |
| --- | --- |
| ![Story reader with Mira's generated adventure and narration and PDF controls](docs/images/demo-reader.jpg) | ![Reading rewards with the first sticker unlocked](docs/images/demo-rewards.jpg) |
| Return to a saved chapter, start narration, or download the book. | Complete the adventure to earn a sticker. |

| Bookshelf | Printable book |
| --- | --- |
| ![Bookshelf with a completed three-chapter adventure and an unfinished story](docs/images/demo-bookshelf.jpg) | ![A5 print preview showing the first chapter and page number](docs/images/demo-print.jpg) |
| Pick up an unfinished adventure or reread a completed one. | Export the selected path as an A5 PDF. |

<details>
<summary>View the illustrated PDF cover</summary>

![A5 PDF cover with a moonlit forest and fox, generated by Automatic1111](docs/images/demo-print-cover.jpg)

</details>

## Features

| Feature | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **My Little Heroes** | Save and edit a character's name, favorite color, and favorite animal. Include those preferences in future stories. |
| **Personalized stories** | Select a hero, theme, and optional idea to generate an original bedtime story with Ollama. |
| **Choose your own adventure** | Three chapters with two decision points, offering 2–3 choices each. Previous chapters and the selected choice shape the next chapter and ending. |
| **Illustrated covers** | Generate watercolor-style covers with the currently loaded Automatic1111 checkpoint. Retry failed illustrations without losing the story. |
| **Our bookshelf** | Reopen saved stories and continue unfinished adventures. |
| **Download as PDF** | Export an A5 book with cover artwork, paginated text, chapter headings, page numbers, and the selected adventure path. |
| **Listen to Story** | Hear gentle-paced narration with an installed device voice or optional local AI speech service. |
| **Reading Rewards** | Unlock stickers after 1, 5, and 10 different stories, and after exploring 3 themes. Each book earns completion credit once. |
| **Local AI settings** | Discover installed completion models and configure localhost service endpoints and voices. Cloud models are excluded from discovery. |

Themes include **Enchanted forest**, **Space explorers**, **Ocean wonders**, and **Magical kingdoms**.

## Technology

- **Frontend:** HTML, responsive CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.
- **Backend:** Node.js and Express, serving the app and proxying local AI requests.
- **Stories:** Ollama `/api/chat` with JSON output.
- **Illustrations:** Automatic1111 `/sdapi/v1/txt2img`.
- **Narration:** Browser Speech Synthesis or local `/v1/audio/speech`.
- **PDFs:** jsPDF, generated in the browser.
- **Storage:** Browser `localStorage`; no database or account required.
- **Tests:** Node.js test runner with mock local AI services.

## Cloud configuration

AI settings lets you select cloud or local providers for text, speech, image, and video, and override cloud model IDs. Provider keys stay on the server. The reader offers voice and pace presets, scene illustrations prompted from the adjacent paragraph, and highlights the current passage. Visual Story mode exports a video with chapter illustrations, cached ElevenLabs or Kokoro narration, and on-screen subtitles. The creation form supports 24 story languages and an optional theme. Non-English narration defaults to Eleven v3. PDFs embed the cover and chapter illustrations and render shaped Unicode text as print-resolution page images. When Hugging Face motion is available, it animates the opening scene. The browser otherwise pans and zooms the illustrations. Keep the reader tab visible while MediaRecorder records the video.

Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in your keys. The server loads this file on startup. Restart after changing it. Keep `.env.local` outside Git.

| Environment variable | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | Primary story generation. The default `OPENROUTER_MODEL` is `openrouter/free`. Ollama takes over if the cloud request fails or does not produce a usable chapter. |
| `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | Primary narration. Set `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` to a voice available to your account. Playback falls back to local Kokoro when configured, then to a device voice. |
| `HF_TOKEN` | Hugging Face token with Inference Providers permission. Defaults are FLUX.1-schnell for covers and Wan 2.2 TI2V for video. Automatic1111 is the cover fallback. |

Hugging Face provides a small free monthly credit allowance. Video may exceed that allowance. Check the estimate and remaining balance before enabling cloud media. StoryTime does not purchase credits.

ElevenLabs audio is saved in the ignored `.storytime-cache/` folder. Identical narration text and voice settings reuse the same file, including across restarts. Concurrent requests for the same narration share one provider call. A changed script or voice produces new audio.

Navigation uses browser URLs and history. Story links reopen books stored in the same browser. Progress bars show when story, chapter, cover, voice, or video generation is waiting for a provider.

## Quick start

Install Node.js 22 or newer and npm, then run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/StoryTime.git
cd StoryTime
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:4173**. Both `npm run dev` and `npm start` run the Express server. Restart it after server-side changes and refresh the browser after frontend changes.

To use another port in PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:PORT = "4180"
npm run dev
```

For a local production-mode run on a machine that shares one GPU between Ollama and Automatic1111, set Ollama to use the CPU:

```powershell
$env:NODE_ENV = "production"
$env:STORYTIME_OLLAMA_GPU_LAYERS = "0"
npm start
```

Leave `STORYTIME_OLLAMA_GPU_LAYERS` unset to let Ollama manage GPU placement.

### Configure Ollama

Install [Ollama](https://ollama.com), start its local service, and download a story model:

```sh
ollama pull llama3.2
```

If Ollama is not already running through its desktop app, run `ollama serve`. The default model is `llama3.2:latest`. In **Local AI settings**, click **Find local models**, select a model, and save.

### Configure Automatic1111

Install [Stable Diffusion WebUI](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui), load a checkpoint, and start it with `--api`.

For a standard Windows installation, add the flag to `webui-user.bat`:

```bat
set COMMANDLINE_ARGS=--api
```

Keep any existing flags and append `--api` if needed. The default address is `http://localhost:7860`. The app uses the currently loaded checkpoint and requests 512 × 640 cover images. Cover generation can be unchecked when creating a story.

### Configure narration

Device narration needs no separate speech server when the browser supports Speech Synthesis and has an installed voice. Choose a voice in the reader's **Reading voice** selector.

For AI narration, run a local Kokoro-compatible server accepting `POST /v1/audio/speech`. Enter its origin and voice ID in **Local AI settings**.

| Setting | Default / example |
| --- | --- |
| Ollama address | `http://localhost:11434` |
| Story model | `llama3.2:latest` |
| Automatic1111 address | `http://localhost:7860` |
| AI speech address | Empty by default; example: `http://localhost:8880` |
| AI speech model sent to service | `kokoro` |
| AI speech voice | `af_heart` |
| AI narration speed | `0.85` |

Ollama and Automatic1111 do not synthesize speech. A grandparent-like voice depends on the speech model or device voice installed; this repository does not ship a dedicated grandparent voice model.

## Your first adventure

1. Create a character in **My Little Heroes** with a name, favorite color, and favorite animal.
2. Select **Tell my story**, choose a theme, and optionally add an idea.
3. Enable **Choose your own adventure** for an interactive story, or leave it off for a complete bedtime tale.
4. Generate the story. If enabled, cover illustration runs after the text is saved.
5. Read together, listen, or download a PDF.
6. Follow adventure choices to the ending and select **We finished this story!** to earn reading credit.
7. Visit **Reading Rewards** to see unlocked stickers and progress.

## Project structure

```text
StoryTime/
├── public/
│   ├── index.html          # App shell
│   ├── app.js              # Heroes, stories, reader, rewards, narration, PDF
│   └── style.css           # Responsive design and decorative illustrations
├── server.mjs              # Express server and local AI proxies
├── tests/api.test.mjs      # API tests with mock services
├── docs/images/            # Project screenshots
├── package.json
└── README.md
```

## API overview

Generation endpoints accept JSON via `POST`. `GET /api/providers` reports which cloud providers are configured. Configured service origins must use `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or IPv6 loopback.

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/api/models` | Discover local Ollama completion models. |
| `/api/story` | Generate a complete story or adventure chapter from hero, theme, history, and choice. |
| `/api/cover` | Request an illustration and return a PNG data URL. |
| `/api/speech` | Return cached or newly generated narration as MP3. |
| `/api/video` | Generate and return a short video with the configured Hugging Face model. |

## Tests and verification

```sh
npm test
```

Automated tests cover narration deduplication, and API tests cover model filtering, hero preferences and adventure history, final chapter choices, placeholder choice rejection, localhost restrictions, and cover response formatting. These tests use mock services and need no downloaded models.

### Live demo

The November 13, 2026 demo ran locally on Windows with `NODE_ENV=production`, Ollama 0.40.16, and `qwen2.5:0.5b` on CPU. The browser created Mira's profile, generated a three-chapter story, submitted two choices, unlocked the first reading sticker, and reopened the saved adventure after reload. The model included Mira, lavender, and foxes. Some passages repeated, and the model sometimes restated earlier events.

Automatic1111 1.9.4 generated a 512 × 640 cover with DreamShaper 8 LCM after its checkpoint warmed up. The cover appeared in the reader and bookshelf and was embedded in the seven-page A5 PDF. Rendered pages confirmed readable text across a page break, page numbering, and inclusion of the selected path.

The device narration control switched between starting and stopping with the Windows voices available in the browser. Audible playback and the optional Kokoro provider were not independently verified.

## Storage, privacy, and current limitations

- Heroes, stories, covers, settings, and rewards are saved in this browser on this device. Clearing site data removes them. There is no account system or cross-device synchronization.
- Download PDFs to preserve books outside the browser. Large cover collections may fill browser storage.
- The server binds to `127.0.0.1`. This is a local development app without internet hosting, authentication, or multi-user configuration.
- AI requests go to configured loopback services. CSS also requests Google Fonts, with system-font fallbacks when unavailable.
- Prompts request gentle stories for ages 4–8, but model output is not guaranteed. Grown-ups should preview stories.
- Adventures are generated chapter by chapter; the saved book retains the chosen path rather than every possible branch.
- Unfinished adventure PDFs include only generated chapters and a continuation note.
- PDF export uses built-in fonts with limited Unicode coverage; Latin-script names and stories work best.
- Speed depends on model size, RAM/VRAM, and other workloads. Cold model loading can take several minutes.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| No models found | Start Ollama, verify its address, and refresh models in Settings. |
| Generation times out | Try a smaller installed completion model, check Ollama logs, and allow it to finish loading. |
| Incomplete story response | Retry or use a model that follows JSON instructions reliably. |
| Cover unavailable | Start Automatic1111 with `--api` and a checkpoint loaded. Use **Illustrate this cover** to retry. |
| No narration | Check installed device voices or the configured speech endpoint and voice ID. |
| Port already in use | Choose another `PORT` and open its matching loopback address. |
| Saved data missing | Use the same browser and origin. Clearing site data or private browsing affects storage. |

## References

- [Ollama API](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md)
- [Automatic1111 API](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui/wiki/API)
- [jsPDF](https://github.com/parallax/jsPDF)

Built for little dreamers and the grown-ups who love them.

projects.description: Investor–business membership platform with compatibility matching, private messaging, pitch-deck uploads, document verification, Stripe subscriptions, and admin review. Built with React, TypeScript, Cloudflare D1/R2, and Vinext. Includes a detailed README and project screenshot.
projects.readme:
# VentureLink

### Opportunity, aligned.

A membership platform connecting ambitious businesses with aligned investors. VentureLink combines profile discovery, compatibility matching, private conversations, pitch decks, document verification, and manual administration in a cohesive, responsive experience.

![VentureLink homepage](docs/images/venturelink-preview.jpg)

**[Visit the deployed site](https://venturelink.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site)** · [Features](#features) · [Getting started](#getting-started) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Launch checklist](#launch-checklist)

> **Status:** The application is deployed privately. Live payment collection requires Stripe configuration and a reachable webhook endpoint. A public GitHub repository does not change the website's private access policy.

## Overview

Finding capital or an investment opportunity is about more than a funding number. VentureLink helps both parties explain their goals, discover relevant profiles, and start a conversation around a shared vision.

- **Businesses** describe their vision, sector, funding requirements, location, stage, and partnership needs.
- **Investors** share investment preferences, budget, location, stage, and the businesses they want to support.
- **Administrators** review registrations and documents, approve or deactivate profiles, and monitor collected subscription revenue.

The interface uses warm neutrals, restrained green accents, generous spacing, consistent cards and forms, and responsive layouts for desktop and mobile.

## Features

| Area | Included behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Registration | Role-specific investor and business onboarding, sector, country, funding budget, stage, and open-ended goals |
| Authentication | Platform-owned ChatGPT sign-in and sign-out with user-specific account records |
| Membership | Stripe Checkout integration for a recurring $10 monthly **or** $10 yearly membership |
| Billing | Stripe Customer Portal integration for billing management and cancellation once configured |
| Discovery | Search by name or description; filter by role, sector, funding amount, country, and verified status |
| Matching | Rank opposite-party profiles and suggest up to five compatible matches |
| Connections | Send a private introduction; acceptance opens further messaging |
| Inbox | Requests, active conversations, persisted message history, and direct replies |
| Live updates | Authenticated Server-Sent Events with periodic change detection and a refresh fallback |
| Pitch decks | Upload PDFs or images and display authorized file links on profile cards and dialogs |
| Verification | Private identity or business-registration documents; manual review controls Verified badges |
| Administration | Registration list, approval, deactivation, verification, and collected-revenue totals |
| Profile reminders | Dashboard prompts to review profile details at the selected monthly or yearly interval |
| Responsive design | Shared navigation, mobile layouts, keyboard-accessible controls, and profile dialogs |

## Membership and access

The current pricing is **$10 per month or $10 per year**, according to the member's preference. There is no additional one-time registration charge.

1. Sign in and prepare an investor or business profile.
2. Save the profile and complete Stripe Checkout when payments are configured.
3. Upload a pitch deck, verification documents, or both as appropriate.
4. An administrator reviews the profile and any verification documents.
5. Approved, paid members can discover real profiles, request connections, and message accepted connections.

Payment, profile approval, and document verification are separate states. Uploading a document does not automatically verify a member. Editing a profile sends it for re-approval and clears its verification badge.

## Matching model

Matches are recomputed from current profile preferences and ranked using:

| Factor | Weight |
| --- | ---: |
| Sector alignment | 40% |
| Investment stage | 20% |
| Country | 15% |
| Proportional funding alignment | 25% |

Only approved, paid profiles from the opposite party are suggested. The dashboard displays at most five matches; fewer appear when the eligible network is smaller. Compatibility scores are heuristics, not investment recommendations or guarantees of funding.

## Messaging and privacy

- Contact email addresses are not published in Discovery or automatically shared in conversations.
- Requests include an introduction; further replies require acceptance.
- Conversation actions check participation and both members' active status.
- Messages and connection records persist in D1.
- Authenticated event streams check for changes every two seconds, reconnect after approximately 50 seconds, and use a 15-second refresh fallback.
- Members choose whether to share personal contact details in a message.

## Uploads and verification

Supported formats are **PDF, JPG, and PNG**, limited to **10 MB per upload**. The server checks MIME types and file signatures before storing files in R2.

- **Pitch decks:** Accessible to their owner, administrators, and approved, paid members when the publishing profile remains active.
- **Verification documents:** Accessible only to their owner and authorized administrators.
- **Verified badge:** Applied manually after a document exists for review. It does not endorse a business or guarantee an investment outcome.

## Pages

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Marketing homepage, illustrative profiles, and membership information |
| `/register` | Investor and business onboarding |
| `/dashboard` | Membership status, connection counts, top matches, and review reminders |
| `/discovery` | Search and filter the network |
| `/inbox` | Connection requests and active conversations |
| `/settings` | Profile details, billing, pitch decks, and verification documents |
| `/admin` | Administrator-only review and revenue monitoring |
| `/privacy` | Privacy, membership, and trust information |

Unknown routes return a 404. Before membership approval, profiles are clearly identified as illustrative and cannot receive real connection requests.

## Technology stack

| Layer | Technology |
| --- | --- |
| Interface | React 19, TypeScript, CSS, Lucide icons |
| Framework | Vinext with Next.js-compatible routing |
| Build | Vite and the Cloudflare Vite integration |
| Runtime | Cloudflare Workers |
| Data | Cloudflare D1 / SQLite, Drizzle ORM and migrations |
| Files | Cloudflare R2 |
| Identity | Sites-managed ChatGPT authentication |
| Payments | Stripe Checkout, Customer Portal, and signed webhooks |
| Live conversations | Server-Sent Events |
| Hosting | Sites |

## Architecture

The React interface calls server routes that validate identity, permissions, and membership before reading or changing data.

```text
Browser / React UI
        |
        +-- /api/platform ------ identity + access checks
        |                              |
        |                              +-- D1: profiles, connections, messages,
        |                              |       uploads, payments, billing
        |                              +-- R2: pitch decks + private documents
        |                              +-- Stripe: checkout + billing portal
        |
        +-- /api/events -------- authenticated conversation-change stream
        |
Stripe -- /api/stripe/webhook -- signature checks + billing reconciliation
```

### Source layout

```text
app/
  platform.tsx                  Shared application views and interactions
  globals.css                   Responsive visual system
  chatgpt-auth.ts                Sign-in and identity helpers
  [section]/page.tsx            Dashboard, Discovery, Inbox, and account pages
  api/platform/route.ts         Profiles, uploads, payments, messaging, admin API
  api/events/route.ts           Authenticated live-update stream
  api/stripe/webhook/route.ts   Signed Stripe webhook processing
components/                     Shared starter UI components
db/                             D1 connection and schema declarations
drizzle/                        SQL migrations and schema metadata
docs/images/                    README project screenshot
scripts/                        Runtime, build, and local-preview tooling
tests/integration.py            Local onboarding and access-control checks
worker/index.ts                 Production Worker entry point
.openai/hosting.json             Sites identity and D1/R2 declarations
```

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- Node.js **22.13.0 or newer**
- npm and Git
- Python 3 for the included local integration checks

### Install and run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/VentureLink.git
cd VentureLink
npm ci
npm run dev
```

The portable development preview normally serves at **http://127.0.0.1:5173**. Use the address printed by the server if a different port is selected.

Local sign-in uses a development-only identity (`seedy@sites.test`). The mock authentication shim is excluded from production builds. Hosted authentication depends on Sites; this repository is not a standalone password-authentication service.

### Initialize local storage

The hosting manifest declares the `DB` D1 binding and `BUCKET` R2 binding. Build once to generate the local Worker configuration:

```bash
npm run build
```

Apply each migration once, in order:

```bash
node --import ./scripts/sites-env.mjs ./node_modules/wrangler/bin/wrangler.js d1 execute DB --local --config dist/server/wrangler.json --persist-to .wrangler/state --file drizzle/0000_flat_lady_mastermind.sql
node --import ./scripts/sites-env.mjs ./node_modules/wrangler/bin/wrangler.js d1 execute DB --local --config dist/server/wrangler.json --persist-to .wrangler/state --file drizzle/0001_equal_warbound.sql
```

Local and production databases are separate. Do not replay applied migrations. After schema changes, run `npm run db:generate`, inspect the generated SQL, and apply only new migrations.

### Runtime configuration

The `.env.example` file lists required configuration names. Configure actual values as hosted runtime secrets or appropriate ignored local runtime configuration.

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Server-side Stripe API access |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Incoming webhook signature validation |
| `ADMIN_EMAILS` | Comma-separated administrator email allowlist |

Never put actual secrets into source files, the hosting manifest, or browser code. Local environment files, runtime state, databases, and build output are ignored by Git.

## Stripe setup

1. Configure the Stripe secret key and webhook signing secret for the runtime.
2. Enable and configure the Customer Portal, including cancellation.
3. Register a publicly reachable snapshot-event endpoint at `/api/stripe/webhook`.
4. Subscribe to:

```text
checkout.session.completed
invoice.paid
invoice.payment_failed
customer.subscription.updated
customer.subscription.deleted
customer.subscription.paused
customer.subscription.resumed
```

5. Test Checkout, renewal, cancellation, failed payments, and portal access in Stripe test mode before activating live payments.

Checkout returns are verified server-side. Webhooks use HMAC signature validation and timestamp tolerance. Invoice identifiers deduplicate recorded payments so an initial checkout and its invoice do not count as two payments. Subscription status controls paid access; admin approval remains independent.

Admin revenue reports recorded collected payments in USD before Stripe fees. It is not a net-revenue report, refund ledger, or monthly recurring revenue calculation.

References: [Stripe webhooks](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks) and [subscription events](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/webhooks).

## Validation

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run build
```

With the development server running and local migrations applied:

```bash
python tests/integration.py
```

The integration script creates a synthetic local profile and verification document. Use only a disposable local development database.

The initial implementation was reviewed on desktop and mobile. **43 local checks** passed across onboarding and uploads, connections, accepted replies and event streams, administration and privacy, webhook signatures, and production page responses. Some checks used temporary local harnesses rather than the committed integration script. Live Stripe transactions have not been exercised because account credentials are still required.

## Deployment

The checkout retains the original Sites identity in `.openai/hosting.json`. Publishing to that project requires the owner's Sites access. For an independent deployment, create a separate Sites project and use its returned identity instead of reusing the original ID.

Production publication packages the Worker and assets, synchronizes the exact source state, applies migrations, and deploys a saved version through Sites. Configure secrets through the hosting platform. Never commit deployment credentials.

The existing deployment is **owner-private**. Publishing this repository does not make the website public, expose its database, or give repository visitors administrator access.

## Launch checklist

- [ ] Connect the intended Stripe account and configure runtime secrets.
- [ ] Configure the Customer Portal and webhook endpoint.
- [ ] Complete end-to-end Stripe test-mode and renewal/cancellation testing.
- [ ] Confirm the $10 monthly / $10 yearly pricing.
- [ ] Explicitly configure the website's audience for customer enrollment.
- [ ] Add the operator's business identity, support contact, and terms.
- [ ] Define verification procedures, document retention, and deletion handling.
- [ ] Review abuse prevention, monitoring, backup, and recovery for expected traffic.

## Current boundaries

- Profile-review reminders appear inside the dashboard; reminder emails are not implemented.
- Bookmarks last for the current page session.
- Verification is manual, not an external identity-verification service.
- The homepage uses illustrative profiles; no demo members are seeded into production.
- The application does not transfer investment funds between members.
- Live payment collection stays disabled until Stripe is configured.

## Licensing

No project-wide open-source license has been selected. Public source availability does not itself grant an open-source license. Included third-party components retain their distributed notices, including those under `vendor/` and `scripts/vite/`.

projects.readme:
# Web App — Godtech

> **Repository category:** Location-based web application

**A location-based spiritual pilgrimage experience that helps people build a lasting practice through sacred-place discovery, prayer offerings, verified visits, and gentle gamification.**

![Godtech pilgrimage map and sanctuary discovery interface](docs/godtech-preview.png)

## Vision

Godtech explores how thoughtful technology can help people return to prayer, reflection, gratitude, and service. The experience is designed for pilgrims and spiritual seekers across traditions. It brings temples, churches, mosques, and other places of worship into one respectful discovery layer while keeping each visit centered on reverence rather than competition.

The product loop is simple:

1. Discover a nearby sacred place on the map.
2. Travel there in person.
3. Choose an intention and make a prayer offering.
4. Check in within the sanctuary's verification radius.
5. Capture a current photo as proof of the visit.
6. Earn light, maintain a devotion streak, and deepen a long-term spiritual journey.

## Current experience

- **Sacred-place discovery** — reads nearby `amenity=place_of_worship` records from OpenStreetMap through the Overpass API.
- **Multi-faith map markers** — recognizes Hindu, Buddhist, Christian, Muslim, Jewish, Sikh, and general sacred places.
- **Place imagery** — displays Wikimedia Commons imagery when the map record provides an `image` or `wikimedia_commons` tag.
- **Location-aware check-ins** — compares the visitor's current coordinates with the selected sanctuary and requires the visitor to be within 250 meters.
- **Prayer offerings** — lets pilgrims dedicate a visit to gratitude, healing, or guidance.
- **Photo proof** — opens the device camera or photo picker and requires a fresh image before a visit can be completed.
- **Pilgrim progression** — rewards verified visits with light points and presents streaks, levels, and progress toward becoming a Devotee.
- **Directions** — opens turn-by-turn directions to the selected sacred place.
- **Responsive design** — provides a map-first desktop layout and a compact, touch-friendly mobile experience.
- **Graceful fallback** — supplies sample sanctuaries when location permission or live map data is unavailable.

## Design direction

Godtech uses a calm spiritual daylight palette rather than a heavy game interface:

- warm ivory for peace and clarity;
- temple gold for devotion and earned progress;
- sacred green for presence and successful verification;
- lotus rose and soft violet for prayer categories and icon backgrounds;
- rounded, clean icon tiles that remain readable on mobile;
- a softened map treatment that keeps sacred-place markers visually prominent.

The interface borrows the immediacy of location-based exploration games while avoiding combative language, scarcity mechanics, or rankings between faiths.

## How verification works

The prototype asks for location only when it needs to center the map or verify a check-in. A pilgrimage is completed when all three conditions are satisfied:

- the pilgrim is within **250 meters** of the selected place;
- a prayer intention has been selected;
- a photo has been captured or chosen on the device.

Current progress and visit metadata are stored in the browser on the pilgrim's device. The photo preview is held only for the active session and is not uploaded to a server in this prototype.

> Production verification should use authenticated accounts, server-side distance validation, durable encrypted photo storage, consent and retention controls, moderation, duplicate-image detection, timestamp checks, and a humane appeal process. GPS and a single image can discourage casual cheating, but they cannot prove physical presence with certainty.

## Technology

| Area | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Interface | Semantic HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript |
| Map | Leaflet |
| Map tiles and places | OpenStreetMap |
| Place search | Overpass API |
| Place photos | Wikimedia Commons links supplied by map records |
| Device capabilities | Browser Geolocation and File/Camera APIs |
| Prototype state | `localStorage` |
| Hosting | OpenAI Sites configuration included in `.openai/hosting.json` |

## Run locally

No build step is required.

```bash
cd dist
python -m http.server 8765
```

Open `http://localhost:8765` in a browser. Location and camera behavior work best in a secure browser context. `localhost` is treated as secure by modern browsers.

## Project structure

```text
Web-App-Godtech/
├── .openai/
│   └── hosting.json       # Sites hosting configuration
├── dist/
│   └── index.html         # Complete application
├── docs/
│   └── godtech-preview.png
├── .gitignore
└── README.md
```

## Responsible product principles

- **Respect every tradition.** Sacred places are presented without ranking one faith above another.
- **Reward consistency, not compulsion.** Streaks should encourage a healthy rhythm and allow rest, travel, illness, and observance differences.
- **Protect sacred spaces.** The app should support venue-specific photography rules and never encourage disruptive behavior.
- **Minimize sensitive data.** Precise location and prayer photos require explicit purpose, short retention, strong access controls, and clear deletion tools.
- **Keep prayer sincere.** Points support the habit; they are not a measure of spiritual worth.
- **Design for safety.** Pilgrims should receive travel, accessibility, opening-hour, and local guidance before visiting unfamiliar places.

## Roadmap

- Account-based pilgrim profiles and cross-device progress
- Durable visit records with encrypted photo evidence
- Server-side geofence and anti-replay validation
- Community-maintained sanctuary pages and photography policies
- Daily, weekly, and monthly devotion journeys
- Wisdom journal and teachings curated with faith advisors
- Accessibility, opening hours, events, and trusted venue contacts
- Private groups for families, congregations, and pilgrimage circles
- Moderation, reporting, consent, retention, and deletion workflows
- Native mobile apps with more reliable camera and location attestation

## Status

Godtech is an interactive product prototype. Its discovery, map, directions, prayer-selection, location-check, photo-selection, and progression flows are functional in the browser. Authentication, cloud photo storage, automated image validation, moderation, and production-grade anti-cheat controls are planned work.

## Contributing

Ideas and contributions are welcome, especially from faith leaders, privacy engineers, accessibility specialists, cartographers, and community safety practitioners. Please approach new features with respect for religious differences and the privacy of visitors and places of worship.

## Data attribution

Map data is © [OpenStreetMap contributors](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright). Place images, when available, are resolved from Wikimedia Commons references present in individual OpenStreetMap records and remain subject to their source licenses.

## License

No open-source license has been selected yet. All rights are reserved by the repository owner unless a license is added later.
